She stared at him, then at the meat. He smiled and reached for the chopping board.

His sword still needed work. Their supper didn't.

The next morning he replaced both broken blades with a plain steel sword. The weapon seller offered a jade-handled ornament; Shi Feng chose sound metal and a grip that fitted his hand. Its price was thirty-two stones, scabbard included. Back in the forest, he repeated the three Iron River movements at reduced force. The point cut cleanly and the steel stayed straight. That was the control he wanted to bring home, rather than another splintered practice weapon.

chapters.title: Until the Road Calls
chapters.html:
Shi Feng returned with the ordinary sword still whole. A morning of Iron River practice had left his wrists warm and his thoughts quiet.

Ling Qingzhu noticed the new weapon before he reached the kitchen.

“You bought a sword?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Unless the seller gave me a very narrow shovel,” Shi Feng replied.

She held out her hand. He passed it over in the scabbard, watching her fingers settle around the handle.

She drew just enough steel to inspect the edge. Her expression stayed calm, but she didn't handle it like someone afraid of cutting herself. Shi Feng noticed that and kept the thought to himself.

“It isn't a refined artifact,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I didn't pay a refined artifact's price,” Shi Feng replied.

“What are you going to do with it?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Practise,” Shi Feng said.

She looked at him for a moment. He'd been carrying a broken wooden blade around his notes lately. A new sword was better than another cracked piece of wood, even if his meridians remained ruined in her mind.

“Then don't practise beside my screen,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Your screen hasn't challenged me,” Shi Feng replied.

“It had better not,” Ling Qingzhu said. “You'd make me buy another.”

He took the sword back, smiling. She went into the kitchen with him and began picking through a bowl of beans. After several breaths, he noticed that she put the good ones in the wrong bowl.

“Are those the beans you've rejected?” Shi Feng asked.

Ling Qingzhu looked down. Then she calmly exchanged the bowls.

“Now they are,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

Shi Feng didn't argue. He wanted supper more than victory.

They ate under the courtyard tree. The weather was growing warmer, and the evenings no longer required a charcoal brazier. Ling Qingzhu complained about a clan letter. An elder still wanted her to receive the consort's messenger about ending the match. The marriage barred a forced royal match, but invitations kept arriving through relatives. She folded the letter and asked whether his sword cost more than his mortar.

He answered. She called him extravagant and took the last piece of bean cake from his plate.

Shi Feng watched her eat it. These little habits were becoming part of his day. He knew exactly how her voice sounded when she was pretending not to care, and which questions meant she wanted him to stay and talk.

He wanted to stay too.

After supper, Ling Qingzhu found the private agreement while arranging her chest. She didn't touch his things. The paper was her own copy, folded beside her correspondence.

She read the extension date and frowned.

“Shi Feng,” Ling Qingzhu called.

He looked up from cleaning the sword.

“The month is nearly over,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I know,” Shi Feng replied.

She waited for him to add something. He waited for her to explain what she wanted. At last, Ling Qingzhu put the agreement on the table between them.

“The regional tournament won't begin immediately,” Ling Qingzhu said. “There are still preparations in the capital. Leaving this house now would be inconvenient.”

“For whom?” Shi Feng asked.

“For both of us,” Ling Qingzhu replied too quickly.

He smiled. Her chin rose a little, warning him not to enjoy that answer too openly.

“Then stay until it's time to leave the capital for the regional tournament,” Shi Feng said. “If either of us wants to end it earlier, we can say so.”

“The same private terms,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

She took a brush and added the new ending to both copies. No intimacy owed, no change to their sleeping arrangements. This extended their private residence together; the registered marriage was a separate matter. Neither promised another payment, and neither opened the old argument about money.

This wasn't how Shi Feng wanted to speak about their future forever. However, it was another evening with her, chosen freely. He wasn't going to reject that because he hoped for more.

Ling Qingzhu finished writing and pushed his copy toward him.

“Don't lose it,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Are you planning to deny it?” Shi Feng asked.

“No,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

Her answer came without hesitation. It pleased him more than her careful wording.

He put the paper away. Ling Qingzhu remained beside the table, running her thumb over the brush handle.

“Will you really go to watch the regional tournament?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“I'll go,” Shi Feng replied.

“It's farther than the river,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I'll buy better shoes,” Shi Feng answered.

She laughed, then told him to stop treating everything as a joke. He promised to consider that after she returned the bean cake.

Behind the folding screen that night, Ling Qingzhu read the new date once more. Outside it, Shi Feng laid the ordinary sword beside his bedding and closed his eyes.

For now, at least, neither of them wanted the room to change.

Ling Shuyun visited two days later with a packet of clan correspondence. Ling Qingzhu tied her veil before opening the gate and remained covered while they sat beneath the pear tree. Ling Shuyun asked about the regional journey, then left the letters and accepted a cup of tea without inspecting the rest of the household.

When the visitor had gone, Ling Qingzhu removed her veil and picked up the wooden blade beside the screen. She made one short turn while reading the first letter. The point cleared the chair by a finger's width. Her wrist had corrected before her eyes left the page.

Shi Feng noticed.

“That's a neat movement,” Shi Feng said.

“I've had an irritating teacher,” Ling Qingzhu said.

She leaned the blade back against the wall. He didn't ask how much she had concealed, and no guest had been present to see it. Her exact realm and the depth behind that ease stayed hers. Shi Feng only guessed that the answer was larger than the small demonstrations she chose to give him.

Later she pushed a loose strand of hair behind her ear while asking about the letters. Shi Feng missed the question. She called his name twice, then smiled at his guilty expression. The sword's neat turn stayed in his thoughts, but so did the way she enjoyed making him forget an ordinary sentence.

chapters.title: The Roots He Needed
chapters.html:
Shi Feng bought the Iron Marrow Stems from Sun Ke after checking their age and condition. The herb seller weighed the usable roots, set aside a soft packet and accepted the ordinary price. Shi Feng kept his hood and face cloth on throughout the purchase. At that counter he was Shen Mo, not Fairy Ling's husband.

The stronger preparation needed several ingredients in the right proportions. He checked his list and headed toward the tower for the rest.

His next stop was Sky Pavilion's ingredient counter. The hall smelled clean, and the herbs rested in sealed trays instead of hanging above a charcoal stove.

He paid more there. He also knew what he was buying.

“Six portions?” Deng Zhi asked.

The counter attendant, Deng Zhi, wore a plain brown robe and carried the steady aura of Bone Refinement. He didn't stare at the hood or ask why a private alchemist needed common bone-strengthening herbs in such quantities.

“Six,” Shi Feng replied. “Dry, without a prepared mixture.”

Deng Zhi checked the boxes and set aside one with a damaged seal before counting the others.

“That one?” Shi Feng asked.

“Returned for inspection,” Deng Zhi replied. “You won't receive it as fresh stock.”

Shi Feng nodded. Honest service didn't need to become a friendship. He paid and accepted the sealed ingredients.

A young man at the next counter was demanding a medicine that would finish Bone Refinement in ten days. His father stood behind him looking increasingly embarrassed.

“Money isn't the problem!” Liang Zhe shouted.

“Ten days won’t finish the bones,” Deng Zhi replied calmly. “Tell me how many you’ve refined. Then I can show you the medicine suited to you.”

The young man lowered his voice. His father leaned toward the counter at once. Shi Feng left them discussing actual cultivation instead of the size of the purse.

Outside, he checked the total. The ingredients took a large part of his recent profit, but he still kept enough money for the next sessions and ordinary expenses. He wouldn't swallow the rent and then act surprised when Gao Yuan knocked.

He thought, Spend heavily where it helps. Don't spend everything everywhere.

The remaining Golden Vein Root from Zhu Shan's earlier payment lay wrapped in his storage bag. With the new stems and common herbs, he could prepare several useful portions for the last golden bones.

He wasn't certain the whole stock would finish the work. No one in Mo Tianheng's known formulas described a skeleton like his. Still, his own progress gave him a sensible estimate.

He'd buy what he needed based on that, not a merchant's miracle promise.

At the furnace, he spent the afternoon making his own medicine. Paid orders were already delivered, and no customer owned any part of these ingredients.

The Golden Vein Root softened slowly. He kept its extraction apart from the tougher stems, then joined the liquids after both reached the right state. The new mortar reduced the stems to even powder without leaving thick pieces at the bottom.

His first portion set too quickly. It formed a hard lump instead of a sound pill.

Shi Feng opened it and checked the center. The herbs' qi remained useful to his physique, but the successful multiplication was missing. He set it aside and reduced the heat for the next attempt.

The second gave two sound pills. The third gave three.

He didn't cheer over five. He recorded the amount, cleaned the vessel, and prepared the next portion while his fingers remembered the correction.

By evening, a modest bottle of useful medicine stood beside a much less attractive jar of failed pieces. Both belonged to him. Neither needed to impress a buyer.

Shi Feng ate a failed portion first and guided the medicinal force into the remaining ordinary traces. Heat spread through his lower back. Another narrow section turned golden, and he stopped to examine the change.

Closer.

The final parts weren't impossible. They were expensive.

He laughed quietly and took a successful pill. Its stronger force followed the same route, giving a much greater advance from the same herbs.

This was why he needed alchemy to improve. His physique let him use failure. His ambitions made success worth pursuing.

Ling Qingzhu was arranging clothes when he returned. She lifted a folded robe from his floor bedding and held it against the light.

“You wear the same sleeve out first,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Then the other sleeve is saving money,” Shi Feng replied.

She lowered it and looked at the ingredient boxes in his hands.

“More medicine?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Some for my own practice,” Shi Feng said.

“Don't leave those under the table,” Ling Qingzhu warned. “I nearly kicked one yesterday.”

“You've challenged the tree and the boxes,” Shi Feng said. “Should I warn the stove?”

Ling Qingzhu threw the folded robe at his chest. He caught it and set the medicine in the kitchen.

When he came back, she was smoothing the rest of his folded clothes. She didn't look at him while doing it.

“Did you sort those?” Shi Feng asked.

“They were taking up space,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

“They still take up space,” Shi Feng said.

“Less badly,” Ling Qingzhu answered.

He smiled and sat on the stool. She passed him a loose tie from one robe and told him to fix it before it fell off.

There was no grand declaration in the room. Her book lay open beside the bed, his sword leaned safely against the corner, and the new medicine waited beyond the kitchen door. He felt happy looking at it all.

Shi Feng thought, I could get used to this for much longer than a few months. He didn't say so. She was arguing with the stubborn fold of his collar, and interrupting would probably make her blame him for it.

Later, when she slept, he took the next portion of medicine. Golden light spread through the last unfinished sections of his skeleton. The flow slowed, then steadied again when he guided it from a different angle.

The end was no longer hidden behind months of uncertain progress. He could see where to put his next step.

The last portion warmed his left hand so strongly that he set it flat on the table. The wood held. He deliberately tightened one finger until a shallow mark appeared, then relaxed it again. Previously, checking his strength often ended with something broken. This time he stopped exactly where he intended.

Cultivation wasn't only filling the body with more force. He needed to remain its master afterward. Xu Changhe's sword notes became more useful each day his bones grew stronger.

He washed the cup and covered the medicine before returning to his bedding. Behind the screen, Ling Qingzhu turned once and settled again. He lay down quietly, already planning which orders to finish before taking a few days for the final refinement.

He'd paid for enough herbs to finish the First Extreme in one secluded push—and with Eastern Palace watchers now asking questions at the city gates, tomorrow morning he would leave the capital by the ridge path and not return until every bone shone gold.

chapters.title: Three Quiet Days
chapters.html:
“You're closing?” Yan Meizhen asked.

“For three days,” Shi Feng replied.

The Bone Refinement buyer looked at her finished order, then at the emptied furnace table. Shi Feng already washed the copper bowl and packed his personal tools. Even Gao Yuan's shouting outside sounded less important with the work done.

“Are you ill?” Yan Meizhen asked.

“No,” Shi Feng said.

“Going somewhere profitable?” Yan Meizhen asked.

“Somewhere quiet,” Shi Feng replied.

Yan Meizhen glanced toward the door as Gao Yuan demanded payment for a cracked stool.

“Then charge extra when you find it,” Yan Meizhen said.

She paid her balance and left. Every promised delivery was finished. Shi Feng refused two new requests that morning instead of taking advances and making customers wait without warning.

He wasn't rich enough to stop working for months. Three days belonged to him, though. He finally earned that much freedom.

The little stone hut stood beyond Hengyun's usual hunting trails. A low ridge hid it from the road, and a dry streambed ran behind the walls. Its owner kept tools there during the busy season and rented it when he could.

Old Man Luo opened the door with a key tied to his belt. He was an elderly Qi Condensation cultivator with a crooked shoulder and no interest in why a hooded man wanted silence.

“Nothing inside belongs to you,” Old Man Luo said.

“I don't want your rake,” Shi Feng replied.

“The last tenant said that too,” Old Man Luo muttered.

He pointed out the old stove, the water jar, and a patched roof. Shi Feng checked them himself, then paid for three days. The price included being left alone.

“If you hear beasts, stay inside,” Old Man Luo warned. “The bigger ones sometimes come down after dark.”

“I'll remember,” Shi Feng said.

“Remember the rake too,” Old Man Luo added.

He took his key and left. Shi Feng listened until the old man's steps faded. Then he walked around the hut and checked the ridge, streambed, and nearest trees.

No one waited nearby. No busy path overlooked the door. This wasn't a grand hidden cave, but he didn't need a legend to sit quietly and cultivate.

He needed walls, privacy, and no furnace owner asking whether the air cost extra.

Before staying there, he returned home once. Ling Qingzhu was waiting with a basket beside the courtyard gate.

“The flower market,” Ling Qingzhu said before he spoke.

“I remember,” Shi Feng replied.

“You looked as if you were going to explain why you forgot,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I was going to say I've finished the deliveries,” Shi Feng replied.

She lifted the basket. “Then come,” Ling Qingzhu said.

They went while the afternoon light still filled the streets. The flower sellers called prices beneath rows of hanging pots. Ling Qingzhu spent a long time comparing two small white-flowered plants, then chose the cheaper one because its roots looked stronger.

Shi Feng said nothing until they left the stall.

“What?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“You counted,” Shi Feng said.

“I inspected,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

“So do I,” Shi Feng said.

“Your inspection always ends in an argument,” Ling Qingzhu answered.

He laughed and took the heavier side of the basket. They bought no grand spirit blossom and attracted no new young master. For once, choosing a plant was only choosing a plant.

At home, they put it near the courtyard wall. Ling Qingzhu insisted it needed morning sunlight. Shi Feng warned that the pear tree might become jealous.

She told him to stop insulting the tree after using its shade every day.

He watched her kneel beside the new pot and press the soil gently. Her black hair slipped over her shoulder. When she looked up to ask for water, he already held the cup.

The warm look she gave him stayed with him after she turned back. Shi Feng thought, I want to return to this. That isn't difficult to understand.

“I'll be away for a few days,” Shi Feng said after supper.

Ling Qingzhu's spoon stopped.

“Another expedition?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“No,” Shi Feng replied. “Some private practice. I've rented a quiet place.”

She looked at the medicine packed beside his ordinary sword. Her expression became guarded. She still thought his meridians ruined, and stubborn practice sounded like a good way to hurt himself.

“Don't let anyone sell you a miracle,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I rented a hut,” Shi Feng replied. “The miracle wasn't included.”

“I'm serious,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“So am I,” Shi Feng answered, more gently.

She lowered her eyes to the bowl. He wasn't asking her permission, and she knew it. Still, she wanted to tell him to stay where she could see whether he was injured.

“When will you return?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“After three days, unless I need to extend the rent,” Shi Feng replied. “I'll send word if I do.”

“Then send word,” Ling Qingzhu said. “Don't make me wonder whether you've fallen in a ditch.”

“I'll avoid the ditches,” Shi Feng replied.

She didn't smile, but she packed a little cooked food for his first day. He accepted it without teasing her. She watched him put the parcel beside his medicine, then fetched a second piece of cloth.

“For the bowl,” Ling Qingzhu said. “The first wrapping isn't thick enough.”

“I'm carrying it, not throwing it,” Shi Feng replied.

“Then carry it properly,” Ling Qingzhu said.

He let her wrap it again. Her fingers worked more carefully than they did while mending his sleeve. She checked the knot twice, then pushed the parcel back without looking up.

“Will you eat?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“Some people forget during practice,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I haven't forgotten a meal you've watched me eat,” Shi Feng replied.

She looked annoyed at having her concern noticed. He put the food away before she could take it back.

At the gate, she stood beneath the pear tree and watched him leave. Shi Feng turned once. She immediately looked toward the new flowerpot, pretending that was what brought her outside.

He smiled and continued down the lane. Three quiet days suddenly sounded longer than they did at the furnace. Still, he wanted to return with the step completed. The stronger he became, the less he would need to accept anyone else deciding his future.

In the hut, Shi Feng laid out the final medicine and sat with his back away from the cold wall. The door was barred. His sword rested beside his knee.

He began with the weaker portions. Their force flowed through his meridians and reached the stubborn unfinished parts of his skeleton. Golden light strengthened along his spine, then moved toward the remaining joints.

The ordinary Bone Refinement ended long ago. This was the second refinement, the taboo change begun by his Ancestral Bone. Every completed section now joined the others more smoothly.

He swallowed another pill.

Heat gathered. He guided it slowly rather than pushing blindly into the last resistant places. One section finished, then another. He could feel exactly which parts remained different.

By midnight, he opened his eyes and checked his hand. The skin looked ordinary. Beneath it, the bones shone gold without a break.

He pressed his palm against a loose stone by the door. It sank into the surface before he released even half his strength.

Shi Feng felt excited. He drew his hand back and examined the shallow mark.

“Still not all of it,” Shi Feng said quietly.

The last change waited deeper in his body. He took out the strongest prepared portion and placed it before him.

Beyond the wall, the night remained quiet. His customers had their medicine. His wife knew where the next three days went. There was nothing left to interrupt the work.

Shi Feng closed his eyes and swallowed.

chapters.title: The First Extreme
chapters.html:
“The rake's still here?” Old Man Luo called through the door.

Shi Feng opened one eye. Morning light entered through the narrow shutter. His final prepared medicine lay nearly finished beside him, and the old hut owner stood outside worrying about farm tools.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“Good,” Old Man Luo said. “I'm going to the lower field. You won't see me until the rent ends.”

“I paid for quiet,” Shi Feng reminded him.

“And you got a whole night,” Old Man Luo replied.

His footsteps moved away. Shi Feng listened until even the scrape of his crooked boot faded down the slope.

Then he closed his eyes again.

The last golden traces gathered near the center of his body. His ribs, spine, limbs, and the small bones of his hands already answered together. Only a few stubborn places still broke that complete feeling.

He took the next pill and let its multiplied medicinal force spread. There was no resistance from the earlier doses. His All-Devouring Physique accepted every portion cleanly, then directed the strength where he needed it.

The final refinement slowed.

Shi Feng didn't panic. He already knew how greedy the last bones were. He gathered the failed pieces left from his private batches and swallowed those too. Their herbs' qi joined the stronger pills, giving what they could without a successful pill's multiplication.

Even the scorched residue mattered here. Nothing medicinal went to waste in his body.

Heat rose through his chest. He steadied his breathing and followed its course inward.

The first remaining section turned gold before noon. It wasn't a flash visible through his skin. Shi Feng felt the change inside, a hard, complete strength replacing the last uneven place along that path.

He guided the force onward.

The next section took longer. His qi moved through all three hundred and sixty-five meridians, feeding the medicine into the refinement instead of letting it scatter through his flesh.

His five Epoch Meridians remained open and alive. The dormancy that made the world call him a cripple was long behind him. Their extraordinary capacity helped him sustain a change that an ordinary Bone Refinement cultivator couldn't even imagine.

Shi Feng thought, I've paid for every part of this. Finish properly.

He didn't rush toward Foundation Establishment. That realm could wait beyond the work already before him. He wanted the complete Extreme, not a nearly finished version he regretted later.

Another pill dissolved. The last Golden Vein Root preparation followed.

The remaining ordinary traces grew thinner.

By afternoon, his whole skeleton felt almost joined. He could follow the gold from his fingers to his shoulders, through his chest, and down into his feet without losing the thread of its force.

Almost wasn't enough.

He stayed seated and continued guiding the medicine. Outside, a bird called once. The old stove clicked as yesterday's heat finally left a loose stone.

Inside his body, the final narrow section changed.

Gold met gold.

For several breaths, Shi Feng forgot the hut entirely.

The force didn't explode outward. It gathered inward, passing through every refined bone before settling into a single complete strength.

His Ancestral Bone no longer stood apart from an unfinished skeleton. All two hundred and six bones were golden. The second refinement was complete.

The First Extreme.

Shi Feng opened his eyes. His heart beat hard with excitement, and he grinned before he could stop himself.

“Finally,” Shi Feng said.

He stood slowly. The movement felt light, but the strength beneath it was frightening. His body wasn't merely a little tougher than yesterday. Every part supported every other part without the earlier unevenness.

He reached for the hut's door bar and stopped before taking it. A careless pull might break it and give Old Man Luo another reason to return. Instead, he lifted the bar gently and stepped outside.

He washed at the basin before testing his strength. His reflection caught his attention. Bone Refinement had improved his looks steadily; with the golden refinement complete, the change was clearer.

His skin was smooth and healthy, his features sharper, and his straight-backed figure held a natural strength. The face was still his own. It simply looked far better than it had during those hungry days in the clan.

Shi Feng rinsed his hands and left the basin. Being handsome wouldn’t test his fist for him.

The ridge stood between the hut and the road. He walked behind it until neither the building nor any path could be seen. A broad, half-buried stone rested beside the dry streambed.

He put one hand against it.

At first he used the amount of force that made the earlier handprint. The surface crumbled immediately. Shi Feng increased it a little, and cracks spread deep through the stone.

He withdrew his hand.

The upper half fell apart.

Shi Feng looked at the broken rock and felt delighted. He didn't need a grand technique to do that. His completed golden bones alone could support terrifying physical force.

Ordinary peers wouldn't even understand the difference until they struck him.

He tested movement next. A small push carried him across the dry streambed farther than he intended. His foot struck the bank, sending loose earth down the slope.

Shi Feng stopped and laughed at himself.

“Not that much,” Shi Feng muttered.

He tried again with less force. This time he landed where he wanted. On the third attempt, his body obeyed smoothly.

Strength had grown. Control needed to follow.

He picked up a fallen twig and held it between two fingers. The first squeeze snapped it. On the next attempt, he held another without leaving a mark. Then he turned it gently and laid it down whole.

Such a little test mattered. If he couldn't touch a cup without breaking it, overwhelming force would become a daily nuisance. He didn't intend to buy new bowls every time he drank.

He repeated the movement until his fingers stopped using yesterday's measure of strength. Walking came next, then turning quickly without digging his heel into the ground. By the time he finished, his body answered the ordinary movements smoothly again.

The First Extreme didn't force him to parade its power. He could keep it still, move normally, and release it when he chose. That pleased him almost as much as the broken stone.

He drew the ordinary sword, but used no great force through its edge. Piercing Current passed through the air. Turning Wave followed, then Returning Tide.

The steel trembled at the final thrust.

He lowered it immediately. The weapon wasn't suited to his full power anymore. He could still practise accuracy, but a serious battle would demand something stronger or a very careful hand.

Shi Feng thought, Foundation Establishment first. Then a refined artifact I can actually use.

He returned to the hut, leaving the broken stone hidden behind the ridge. There were no watchers, cheering hunters, or rumours to explain. The capital could keep laughing at its cripple a little longer.

His achievement belonged to him before it belonged to anyone else's opinion.

He ate the food Ling Qingzhu packed and drank water slowly. The rice was plain. She wrapped it too tightly, and one corner stuck to the cloth.

He smiled while peeling it free.

He wanted to tell her he'd succeeded. He also knew what questions would follow. The complete story reached far beyond a good training session: awakened meridians, taboo golden refinement, the devoured spirit in the ring.

He wasn't ready to pour all those secrets onto their supper table.

That didn't make the wish disappear.

After eating, he examined his cultivation inwardly. The First Extreme remained steady. No ordinary trace lingered in his skeleton, and the strength moved cleanly when he guided it.

He didn't find a reason to delay the next realm now. Meridian Opening went beyond the known limit. Qi Condensation filled the capacity he built. Both stages of Bone Refinement reached their full completion.

Every step was his own foundation for what came next. Shi Feng folded the empty food cloth, set it beside the sword, and sat again. He wouldn't enter Foundation Establishment carelessly while still excited from breaking a rock.

First he'd steady the new force. Then he'd take the next step.

Outside, the ridge hid the hut from the road. Inside, Shi Feng closed his eyes and let his completed golden bones answer together.

chapters.title: His Own Foundation
chapters.html:
“No more waiting,” Shi Feng said.

He sat inside the stone hut with the door barred. The ordinary sword lay beside him, and the last of his prepared food was covered near the water jar. His completed golden bones remained steady after a full night's adjustment.

The First Extreme was finished. He could feel it in every movement.

Now came Foundation Establishment.

He slowed his breathing and gathered his qi inward. All three hundred and sixty-five meridians answered. The force moving through them was vast, but he didn't let it rush ahead without direction.

This wasn't a battle where overwhelming an opponent solved the problem. He was building the next step inside his own body. Every part needed to join properly.

Mo Tianheng's remembered knowledge included the ordinary process. Shi Feng studied it before coming here. He knew the known foundation grades, from Mortal to Divine, and how earlier cultivation affected the result.

He didn't select a grade by wishing for its name. His meridians, condensed qi, and completed golden bones were already there. Whatever they could build, he'd build completely.

The first change came quietly. Qi that once spread easily through his body gathered into a denser flow. His meridians carried it without strain, and the golden skeleton supported the growing pressure.

Shi Feng guided it through one complete circuit, then another. The force returned cleaner each time. He didn't lose the capacity he built during Qi Condensation. He was changing the way that strength held together.

The hut remained still. There was no lightning above the roof and no sky-shaking beam announcing his secrets. A lightning tribulation waited at the step toward Golden Core, not here.

Shi Feng's attention stayed inside. One uneven current tried to move ahead of the others. He slowed it and matched the whole flow before continuing.

His five Epoch Meridians answered with tremendous force. For a moment he understood why attempting this without complete preparation would've been foolish. An ordinary body might not sustain what those meridians carried.

His golden bones did.

He thought, This is why I didn't leave them unfinished. The thought brought satisfaction, but he didn't linger over it. The process wasn't done.

He drew in the surrounding spiritual qi and refined it steadily. The hut's thin walls offered little shelter from noise, but the ridge kept passing travelers away. Nobody came to ask what he was doing.

For once, quiet stayed quiet.

The gathered force settled deeper. His body no longer treated the stronger qi as a temporary surge. It moved with his intention, stable and clear.

Shi Feng felt a firm support beneath every circuit. It wasn't an object he could pull out and display. It was the result of every completed stage joining into the beginning of a new realm.

His foundation took shape.

He checked the descriptions he knew. A Mortal foundation couldn't explain the force he felt. Neither could the better grades in the remembered accounts. Even the descriptions of Divine foundations failed to match the depth before him.

Shi Feng didn't invent a grand title to cover what he couldn't measure.

“My foundation,” Shi Feng said quietly.

That was enough for now.

He guided another circuit through it and waited for any unsteady place to appear. None did. His meridians carried the transformed qi smoothly, and his skeleton held its complete strength beneath the flow.

Early Foundation Establishment.

The words came with a surge of delight. He opened his eyes and grinned at the empty hut.

For months, the world called him a cripple. Now he stood in the realm required to compete beside the kingdom's proudest young cultivators.

They didn't need to know it today.

He stood and took the plain sword. This time he guided a thin stream of the new qi toward it, then stopped before the steel began to complain.

The difference was clear immediately. Even a small amount carried more force and finer control than his previous qi. The ordinary weapon could still cut, but it couldn't let him use the full change safely.

A refined artifact would.

He set the sword down and tested the flow through his fingers instead. A loose pebble rose from his palm, wavered, and dropped. Shi Feng caught it before it struck the floor.

“Again,” Shi Feng murmured.

He tried with less force. This time the pebble stayed steady for several breaths before he released it deliberately.

Stronger qi didn't remove the need to learn his own control. However, the response was far clearer now. Adjustments that previously fought the limits of Bone Refinement became possible without forcing them.

He spent the next hours practising simple movements and steady circulation. No new grand technique, no leap to the next stage. He wanted early Foundation Establishment to remain solid before using it in a real fight.

He tested the new flow through another slow circuit. It remained steady. The breakthrough hadn't removed the need for practice, but tomorrow he would wake with this strength still his own.

At sunset, he went behind the ridge and tested one short palm strike against the broken stone left from yesterday. The remaining stone split cleanly. He used far less effort than before.

Shi Feng looked at his hand with quiet satisfaction. Ordinary Foundation Establishment opponents weren't going to trouble him. Even an early Golden Core cultivator would face a very different battle from Cao Wenshu's.

He didn't need to seek one out merely to prove it.

Old Man Luo returned the next morning and stopped beside the hut's open door.

“Done?” Old Man Luo asked.

“For now,” Shi Feng replied.

The hood covered his face again. His qi remained withdrawn, giving the old man no open display to recognize.

Old Man Luo inspected the stove, water jar, and tools. He counted the rake twice.

“Nothing broken,” Old Man Luo said, sounding almost disappointed.

“You charged for a hut, not rubble,” Shi Feng replied.

“Some tenants don't know the difference,” Old Man Luo said.

He accepted the key and waved Shi Feng toward the road. Neither man offered to become the other's lifelong acquaintance.

Shi Feng returned to the capital before noon. The familiar streets looked the same. A noodle seller shouted, two guards argued over a cart, and someone outside a wine shop claimed his brother could defeat the kingdom's tenth-ranked young genius.

The world hadn't changed because Shi Feng entered a new realm.

He had changed enough.

Ling Qingzhu opened the courtyard gate before he knocked twice.

“Three days,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I returned in three,” Shi Feng replied.

“I was counting,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“So was Old Man Luo,” Shi Feng replied. “He cares deeply about his rake.”

Ling Qingzhu stared at him.

His face had changed. The last faint unevenness left by his old illness was gone, and his features seemed clearer beneath the road dust. When he smiled, she forgot the complaint she'd prepared about how long he'd been away.

Then she turned toward the kitchen too quickly.

Shi Feng looked past her at the covered rice.

“Is it burning?” Shi Feng asked.

“No,” Ling Qingzhu replied. “You can stop looking at the doorway.”

“I was looking at supper,” Shi Feng said.

That made it worse. She stepped aside, annoyed with herself. He had come home without a new wound, and she'd noticed his face before checking his sleeves.

“Was the practice useful?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Very,” Shi Feng replied.

She studied his face. He looked happier, and his voice held an ease she hadn't heard before. Still, he didn't release qi or claim restored meridians. She took it as satisfaction from stubborn effort.

“Then wash before eating,” Ling Qingzhu said.

She'd left rice covered in the kitchen. Shi Feng set his bag down and smiled. In the bottom of that bag, the black ring waited.

For the first time, he had the realm needed to open it. He could finally learn what storage remained behind that stubborn seal.

He would examine it properly when the kitchen was quiet.

chapters.title: An Empty Chest Was Useful
chapters.html:
“If you're selling the chest, open it,” Shi Feng said.

Tang Sen hugged the little wooden box tighter. The secondhand stall stood beside the west market wall. Broken lamps, old medicine scoops, and mismatched bowls filled every space around his feet.

“Opening it lowers its value,” Tang Sen replied.

“So does finding nothing inside,” Shi Feng said.

The Qi Condensation seller looked wounded. He claimed the box came from a dead cultivator's estate, which apparently excused the lack of a key and made every scratch expensive.

“Maybe there's a pill formula,” Tang Sen suggested.

“Then you should open it,” Shi Feng replied.

“Maybe there isn't,” Tang Sen admitted.

Shi Feng bought a plain medicine scoop instead. It cost little and had no mystery attached. Tang Sen tried to sell him the box again while wrapping the scoop, but Shi Feng left without listening.

He already had enough mystery in a black ring.

That evening, Ling Qingzhu went to answer a clan letter at a nearby family residence. She said she'd return before the late bell and reminded Shi Feng not to leave supper uncovered. He put a lid over the bowl before she finished speaking.

“Like this?” Shi Feng asked.

“Don't be irritating,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

“Then stop giving me practice,” Shi Feng said.

She left with a cold look that didn't hide her smile. Alone in the kitchen, he took the black ring from its wrapping. It looked exactly as it did when he carried it out of the ruin: plain, dark, and unimpressive beside the more decorative rings sold in the market.

Mo Tianheng's spirit no longer hid within it. That attempted possession ended when Shi Feng's physique devoured the attacker. The alchemy knowledge and remembered experience were already inside his mind.

Opening storage wouldn't grant them a second time.

He guided a small stream of Foundation Establishment qi into the ring. The old resistance weakened immediately. A space beyond its surface became clear to his senses.

Shi Feng's heart beat faster.

“So that's what it was holding,” Shi Feng murmured.

The storage was far larger than his cheap bag. Even mostly empty, it would hold furniture, supplies, and many months of ingredients without forcing him to arrange every packet around his bedding.

Three travel chests rested inside. Several old tools lay beside them, along with a small pouch and two sealed herb packets.

Inside the three chests he found clean medicine jars, an empty sorting tray, and a balanced pair of furnace tongs.

He opened the pouch.

Ninety-six spirit stones.

Shi Feng counted them once and laughed quietly. A formidable Profound Heaven alchemist's spirit tried to steal his body, and the money left behind wouldn't pay for a grand feast at Yuelan Terrace.

He didn't feel cheated. He already gained the attacker's expertise. The empty space alone was an excellent treasure.

The herb packets held modest materials he could use in ordinary preparations. Their seals preserved them well, but there was no divine root or impossible fruit waiting to carry him through three more realms.

He checked each before putting it aside. Old didn't automatically mean powerful. Sometimes old meant a packet that needed careful inspection.

The tools were sound. The tongs gripped evenly, and a narrow scraper would be useful for cleaning furnace seams. None was a grand refined artifact that he couldn't understand.

Shi Feng thought, Good. Things I can use without needing another adventure first.

He tested the space with the new medicine scoop. A brief touch of qi put it inside the ring. Another brought it back to his palm.

The first retrieval was clumsy. The scoop appeared at an angle, and he nearly dropped it. On the next try, he pictured its position more carefully before releasing the qi.

It settled into his hand properly.

He repeated the process with a bowl, a bundle of herbs, and one empty travel chest. Each needed attention, but none fought him. Foundation Establishment let him use the ring as intended.

The cheap storage bag still had its uses. He could carry ordinary purchases in it without showing anyone that the black ring held much more. There was no reason to parade the ruin's main treasure before the market.

He moved his personal tools into the ring, leaving customer ingredients clearly separated. Keeping space didn't mean forgetting ownership. A large part of his kitchen shelf became empty.

Shi Feng looked at it with satisfaction. That might be the simplest benefit of a spatial treasure: he could finally find the salt without moving medicine boxes.

He also checked what the storage could safely hold. Dry goods stayed dry; a covered water jar remained upright where he put it. There was no living beast inside, and he didn't try to make the ring swallow one merely to answer a curiosity. He could learn the space's useful limits without testing every dangerous possibility tonight.

The main advantage was simple. Previously, every large purchase meant another bundle, another trip, or leaving supplies where a landlord could inspect them. Now he could keep his own materials with him. For an alchemist who worked in rented rooms, that freedom mattered.

He placed the ninety-six stones with his own funds, then transferred the unused chests back into storage. They weren't useless merely because they were empty. He could fill them himself.

Ling Qingzhu noticed the clearer kitchen shelf when she returned before the late bell.

“You finally moved those boxes,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“They aren't beside your feet now,” Shi Feng replied.

“Good,” Ling Qingzhu said. “I was going to move them myself.”

“Into the well?” Shi Feng asked.

“Only the irritating ones,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

He smiled and took down the salt jar without shifting anything first. She watched, then gave a little nod as if he had finally obeyed sensible household instruction.

After she retired behind the screen, he opened Xu Changhe's sword notes and checked the passages on channeling Foundation Establishment qi through a blade. The ordinary steel beside him could no longer support what his new realm offered.

The next morning, Shi Feng returned to the south-street weapon shop under his hood and face cloth. The weapon-shop master first offered a gilded sword, then brought out a plain refined artifact when Shi Feng asked for sound formation channels instead of a beast's head on the hilt.

In the enclosed practice yard, Shi Feng guided a thin stream of Foundation Establishment qi through the blade. Its spirit channel answered without the shudder of ordinary steel. He didn't test his maximum strength; he needed a reliable blade for the tournament platform, not another shattered sample.

Using the ninety-six stones from the black ring and twenty-four from his reserve, he paid the one-hundred-and-twenty-stone price in coin, slipped the wrapped refined artifact into the ring in the side lane, and kept his ordinary scabbard at his waist on the walk to the furnace yard.

That afternoon he tested a basic Golden Core formula from Mo Tianheng's memory. Even with Foundation Establishment qi, the binding separated before the shell formed. He recorded the limit calmly and locked the furnace door—because outside in the lane, Gao Yuan was already waiting with word of a mid Foundation Establishment buyer seeking Returning Breath Pills before the royal qualification list went up.

chapters.title: The Flame Held
chapters.html:
“Don't open that door,” Shi Feng said.

Gao Yuan’s hand stopped on the latch.

“The charcoal delivery’s here,” Gao Yuan called.

“Leave it outside,” Shi Feng replied.

Gao Yuan lowered the sack carefully. One black lump rolled against the threshold. He caught it with his boot before it knocked the wood again.

The landlord grumbled but withdrew. Inside, the copper furnace held a steady low heat. Shi Feng sat before it with three prepared extracts and an empty tray.

For the first time, he was making a Returning Breath Pill with the qi needed to sustain it properly.

The medicine served Foundation Establishment cultivators recovering spent qi. It wasn't a Golden Core pill and earned no Sky Pavilion Mark. Still, it was a clear step beyond the common recovery pills that kept his earlier business alive.

He knew the formula from Mo Tianheng's devoured spirit. He also knew how the stages should feel. Now his own body could keep the separated medicinal forces stable long enough to try the full process.

That didn't mean he could stop paying attention.

The first extract entered cleanly. Shi Feng guided the second along the furnace's outer curve before bringing it toward the center. His new qi held both without spreading thin.

The difference excited him. He didn't let the excitement move his fingers faster.

When the third extract joined, the mixture grew heavy. Previously, this stage pulled his control apart. Now he could feel where the forces resisted each other and adjust the flow before they broke loose.

The joining began.

A round shape emerged, then collapsed on one side. Shi Feng stopped the fire and lifted the lid. One misshapen lump rested in the bowl.

He examined it, annoyed but not surprised. His qi sustained the process. His final turn closed the shell too soon.

“A hand mistake,” Shi Feng said quietly.

That was better than an impossible realm limit. A hand mistake could be corrected today.

He swallowed the cooled lump to recover its raw herb qi, then reset the fire.

On the next attempt, he delayed the closing turn. The inner medicine settled first, then the shell gathered around it. He let the heat fall slowly instead of opening the furnace as soon as the pill looked round.

Two sound pills emerged.

Shi Feng held one beneath the lamp and split it. The center was even. Its medicinal force remained firmly bound instead of drifting out in a sharp, unstable smell.

He felt pleased enough to laugh.

“About time,” Shi Feng murmured.

Months of remembered expertise finally met qi strong enough to use this simple portion of it. He hadn't become Mo Tianheng overnight. He'd taken one formula from memory and made it work with his own hands.

He swallowed the opened pill and tested the effect after spending some qi on controlled movements. The recovery was stronger and steadier than the common medicine.

It worked.

He made another attempt before calling the session finished. This one produced two sound pills and a cracked third. The crack came from cooling too quickly near the furnace's uneven side.

He marked that spot for the next firing. A better realm didn't repair the copper bowl.

Gao Yuan was waiting when he opened the door. The landlord leaned forward, sniffing the changed medicinal scent.

“New pill?” Gao Yuan asked.

“A practice batch,” Shi Feng replied.

“Expensive?” Gao Yuan asked.

“Would you charge the door more if I said yes?” Shi Feng replied.

Gao Yuan looked offended. “I'm interested in your success,” Gao Yuan said.

“So is your rent,” Shi Feng replied.

The landlord gave up pretending and asked whether the new medicine could be offered to paying customers. Shi Feng said not yet.

He had successful pills, but he wanted several consistent batches before promising anyone a collection date. Selling the first good result as a reliable service would turn practice into an angry queue.

“Others announce a new medicine as soon as they get one pill,” Gao Yuan said.

“Buy from them,” Shi Feng replied.

“I don't need medicine,” Gao Yuan said quickly.

“Then let me work,” Shi Feng said.

Gao Yuan sighed and went back to counting charcoal sacks.

Over the following days, Shi Feng kept his existing commissions and reserved short sessions for the new formula. The common recovery pills became easier to manage with Foundation Establishment qi. He could split his attention between the flame and the binding without either slipping away.

He didn't enlarge every batch at once. Reliable work paid for the practice. Practice would eventually give him better work.

The Returning Breath Pill improved from uncertain pairs to several sound pills per attempt. Some still failed. He studied each failure, consumed the medicine safely, and changed the next attempt where the actual fault lay.

One batch failed because the extract was too thick. Another cracked after a hurried cooling. Those were different mistakes, and he treated them differently.

Mo Tianheng's memories made the answers easier to find. Shi Feng's own fingers learned to avoid needing those answers so often.

At the end of the fifth day, he set two successful batches beside each other. Their strength and binding matched closely.

He smiled. Now he had something worth letting a customer inspect.

Before offering it, he checked how the medicine behaved after storage. One pill stayed in an ordinary sealed bottle for a day. Another stayed in the old ring's clean jar. He opened both and compared their scent, surface, and binding. Neither lost strength in a way that would spoil an honest sale.

He also wrote the intended use clearly. It recovered spent qi for Foundation Establishment cultivators. It didn't promise a breakthrough, heal every internal injury, or turn a Bone Refinement buyer into a higher-realm expert. Those extra claims might bring faster sales. They'd also bring people expecting miracles he never made.

His business needed customers who returned because the medicine worked, not because they wanted their spirit stones back. He put the good samples away and planned a small trial order. A larger promise could wait until the first buyer knew exactly what the pill did.

Duan Li came to inspect the first trial order after Shi Feng had matched two batches. The mid Foundation Establishment escort manager wore a faded burn along his neck and looked unimpressed by the copper furnace.

“My old alchemist raised his price,” Duan Li said.

“Did he improve the medicine?” Shi Feng asked.

“He improved his carriage,” Duan Li said.

Shi Feng nearly laughed. They agreed on eight Returning Breath Pills, with ingredients supplied, a fee for the work and any additional successful pills divided as stated on the slip. Shi Feng tested the sample before promising the collection.

The first commission produced eleven sound pills. Duan Li took his eight, checked their binding and paid without another speech about the furnace. Shi Feng kept three and the usable failures. The medicine served Foundation Establishment. It earned no Mark and made no claim to do so.

After the customer left, Shi Feng reserved a short session for the Golden Core formula. This time he held its separated extracts longer before the joining failed. He marked the improvement honestly. It was progress, and still not medicine to sell.

He went home before the rice cooled. Ling Qingzhu asked whether the new preparation worked, and he said it did—and as they finished supper, the palace drums sounded from the central ward to announce that tomorrow morning the ten standing names for the Great Kingdom Tournament qualification would be posted on the capital square.

chapters.title: Three Places
chapters.html:
“Move your elbow!” Gao Min, a tall youth, shouted.

“Move your face!” Liu Tong, his companion, shouted back.

Shi Feng waited until both finished arguing, then stepped around them. The new qualification notice hung beneath the royal seal at the capital square. A crowd of young cultivators pressed close enough to make reading it difficult.

Foundation Establishment remained the minimum realm. The eligible birth years were listed beside the registration dates. Three representatives would leave Great Liang for the regional Great Kingdom Tournament.

Three places.

Shi Feng read the ranked list attached below. Crown Prince Sima Yu stood first, late Foundation Establishment. Ling Qingzhu stood second. Her exact cultivation wasn’t listed. People called her strong and unfathomable; few could say more. Han Zong, a spear user at mid Foundation Establishment, stood third.

The list continued through ten names. Gao Zhen held the tenth place at early Foundation Establishment.

These were the standing candidates. Challenges during the qualification period would decide who kept the places. Shi Feng looked at his wife's name for a moment longer.

She never told him her actual cultivation. The notice named her position and kept the rest private, while she still asked whether his ordinary sword could survive a tree.

He wasn't offended. She had her own secrets, and he carried more than a few. Still, he thought, I'll remember that the next time she pretends a branch is difficult.

Yu Cheng sat beside the registration table with a stack of fresh slips. Shi Feng recognized the clerk from the earlier notice. The man looked no happier now that more applicants wanted answers.

“Unranked candidates challenge tenth first,” Yu Cheng explained to a waiting youth. “Win, and you're on the standing list. Then you may challenge a higher place under the announced rules.”

“Must I fight ninth after tenth?” Gao Min asked.

“No,” Yu Cheng replied. “You can challenge third if you think you can win.”

Several people laughed. The youth flushed and stepped aside.

Shi Feng approached the table.

“Three representatives only?” Shi Feng asked.

“Three,” Yu Cheng replied. “Not ten, not everyone whose uncle knows a minister. Three.”

“And a third-ranked candidate can stop once the position is secure?” Shi Feng asked.

“If he keeps it until qualification closes,” Yu Cheng said. “Someone else can still challenge him.”

Shi Feng nodded. That was clear enough.

He didn't need Great Liang's championship to reach the regional arena. A qualifying place would bring him to the same road. Sima Yu's name above the list represented another matter entirely.

The prince ordered men to kill him. Shi Feng didn't forget those orders because a ranking notice used respectful titles.

He'd settle that grudge where the prince's household couldn't end a fight by shouting his rank. For now, he came to understand qualification, not attack a guarded royal carriage in a public square. Yu Cheng looked at his face more carefully and recognized him.

“You again,” Yu Cheng said.

“I can read twice,” Shi Feng replied.

The clerk glanced at his ordinary sword and shook his head. He didn't bother repeating the old speech about brawlers watching from the street.

“Registration opens in ten days,” Yu Cheng said. “Birth record first. Cultivation verified before a challenge proceeds, in the arena. Don't stand here arguing with me today.”

“I wasn't going to,” Shi Feng replied.

He left before the clerk found a reason to object to that too.

Two young cultivators were discussing Han Zong beside a tea stall. One held a short spear wrapped in expensive cloth. The other kept nodding as if he personally taught the third-ranked candidate.

“Seven people challenged him last season,” Gao Min said. “Not one forced him back three steps.”

“His spear art came from a sect visitor,” Liu Tong replied.

“His clan bought it,” Gao Min said. “Same thing.”

Shi Feng ordered tea and listened. Both men were at Bone Refinement, and their knowledge became less certain the longer they talked. Soon Han Zong's single spear art became three inherited arts and a secret method learned in a forbidden valley.

Shi Feng drank his tea and left before the valley grew a hidden dragon too. The actual ranking and realm mattered. Street boasting could stay at the stall.

Across the square, another notice listed the nearby Great Sects: Martial Palace, Hundred Flower Valley, and Artificer Hall. Their representatives would watch the regional tournament, not spend weeks testing every hopeful in Great Liang. A grey-bearded father pointed at the names while lecturing his son.

“Reach the regional arena first,” Chen Sheng said. “Then you can dream about a sect.”

“Artificer Hall takes fewer warriors,” Chen Lu complained.

“Then become one worth taking,” Chen Sheng replied.

Shi Feng paused at that. Xu Changhe carried a sword and enforced the sect's rules. His legacy wasn't a reason to pretend Shi Feng suddenly preferred crafting over fighting or alchemy. It was a connection to a place he intended to see.

He already chose that road for himself. First came qualification, then the surrounding kingdoms' strongest young cultivators. He wouldn't ask a dead elder's name to do the walking for him.

The father and son continued arguing. Shi Feng left the square with the notice folded beneath his sleeve and a much clearer idea of the next month. Three places sounded few to the crowd. He only needed one.

Ling Qingzhu found him reading the notice copy at home.

“You went to the square?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

Her eyes moved to the ranked list. She didn't look surprised by her own position.

“Second,” Shi Feng said, touching the paper.

“For now,” Ling Qingzhu replied.

“Should I bow before serving rice?” Shi Feng asked.

“You should serve it before it goes cold,” Ling Qingzhu said.

He laughed and put the notice away. She sat across from him, watching his expression more closely than she intended.

“Does it bother you?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“What?” Shi Feng replied.

“My cultivation,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“No,” Shi Feng replied.

She relaxed, then noticed how quickly he answered.

“You could at least think first,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Would you prefer I became bothered?” Shi Feng asked.

“No,” Ling Qingzhu said sharply.

“Then don't complain about a good answer,” Shi Feng replied.

Her mouth curved before she looked down at the bowl. He was relieved she didn't treat the notice as an excuse to lecture him. She was relieved he didn't become gloomy beside her realm.

Neither knew how incomplete the other's understanding remained.

After supper, Shi Feng took out his old birth record. The folded paper carried the proper clan mark and enough wear to prove it hadn't been made yesterday. His age fell within the published eligible years.

No obstacle there.

Ling Qingzhu saw the paper beside his notes and frowned.

“You're not registering to fight, are you?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

She stared at him. “Foundation Establishment is required,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I read that,” Shi Feng replied.

“Shi Feng,” Ling Qingzhu said, suddenly serious, “this isn't a stall argument. Someone can really hurt you.”

He looked at her. Concern lay beneath the sharpness, and he liked that even if she understood very little of his strength.

“I won't register without being able to fight,” Shi Feng replied.

She studied his calm face. He didn't explain further, and she finally shook her head.

“Then don't make promises just because people laughed,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I don't,” Shi Feng replied.

He folded the birth record carefully. In the ring, his refined artifact sword waited beside the medicine supplies.

Tenth first. Third afterward.

That was enough of a route. He checked the registration date once more and laid the paper beneath his work notes. Until then, he still had commissions to finish. Becoming a representative wouldn't pay Gao Yuan's rent before the balance was due, and the furnace owner wasn't likely to accept tournament ambitions as payment.

chapters.title: The Price of Royal Favour
chapters.html:
“I need the advance back,” Yan Meizhen said.

Shi Feng looked at the unopened ingredient box between them. The Bone Refinement buyer sat very straight, without her usual teasing smile. Outside the furnace room, Gao Yuan kept finding reasons to walk past the door.

“The ingredients haven't been used,” Shi Feng replied. “What's changed?”

“Someone asked where I buy medicine,” Yan Meizhen said.

“Many people do,” Shi Feng replied.

“This one wore the Crown Prince's household mark,” Yan Meizhen said.

Shi Feng's expression stayed calm beneath the cloth. His eyes moved toward the door when Gao Yuan's footsteps stopped again.

“What did he want?” Shi Feng asked.

“To know your name, your customers, and how much you earn,” Yan Meizhen replied. “He also suggested our hunting company might lose road permits if we bought from an unsuitable supplier.”

“Meaning me,” Shi Feng said.

Yan Meizhen nodded. She didn't dress it as regret or friendship. Her company needed to travel, and a private alchemist wasn't worth a quarrel with the prince's servants.

Shi Feng returned the unused advance and ingredient box. The lost work annoyed him, but he didn't blame her for protecting her own purse.

“What did you tell him?” Shi Feng asked.

“That I know Master Shen through a medicine peddler,” Yan Meizhen replied. “Which is what I know. I didn't invent a family history for you.”

“Good,” Shi Feng said.

“Don't misunderstand,” Yan Meizhen added. “If someone offers enough trouble, I won't pretend I know less than I do.”

“I didn't ask you to,” Shi Feng replied.

She looked at him for a moment, then stood. Her disappointment was real. So was her decision to leave.

Duan Li's message arrived an hour later. He postponed the next Returning Breath Pill order until his merchant house finished an unexpected inspection.

The message didn't mention the Crown Prince. It didn't need to.

Shi Feng put it beside Yan Meizhen's canceled order and looked at the empty afternoon. Sima Yu's men weren't merely asking questions now. They were reaching the people whose money kept the furnaces lit.

That was a real consequence, not a distant threat. Gao Yuan entered without his usual cheerful demand.

“Master Shen,” Gao Yuan said quietly, “I don't want guards searching my rooms.”

“Neither do your tenants,” Shi Feng replied.

“Perhaps you'd better accept whatever offer they make,” Gao Yuan said.

“What offer?” Shi Feng asked.

The landlord looked toward the gate. A man in a dark robe was already crossing the yard. The small golden mark at his waist made two apprentices hurry aside.

Zheng Jian carried mid Foundation Establishment cultivation and the confidence of someone accustomed to speaking for a prince. He entered the room without waiting for permission.

“Master Shen,” Zheng Jian said. “His Highness appreciates useful talent.”

Shi Feng remained seated. “Then name the price,” Shi Feng replied.

Zheng Jian glanced at Gao Yuan. The landlord disappeared so quickly his sleeve caught the doorframe.

“Medicine for the household,” Zheng Jian said. “Priority over your street customers. Formulas registered with our steward. Your face and real name given when requested.”

“And payment?” Shi Feng asked.

“His Highness's protection,” Zheng Jian replied.

“I asked for payment,” Shi Feng said.

Zheng Jian's smile cooled. He looked at the ordinary copper furnace as if that should remind its owner to be humble.

“You work in a rented room,” Zheng Jian said. “Don't mistake a few buyers for a foundation no one can shake.”

“Then why does your household need my medicine?” Shi Feng asked.

“Because I was sent to offer you a chance,” Zheng Jian replied.

“Keep it,” Shi Feng said.

The room became quiet. Outside, Gao Yuan stopped pretending not to listen.

Zheng Jian stared at the hood. He couldn't see the face beneath it, and the man released no open qi for him to judge. That made the refusal more irritating.

“You have until tomorrow evening,” Zheng Jian said. “After that, don't expect anyone to keep buying.”

“Are you buying today?” Shi Feng asked.

“No,” Zheng Jian said.

“Then you're taking a customer's seat,” Shi Feng replied.

Zheng Jian rose slowly. Anger sharpened his eyes, but he didn't attack inside a crowded rental yard. He came to make the man submit, not start a public fight before learning who stood behind the hood.

He left without bowing.

Gao Yuan waited until the gate closed before showing his face again.

“You could've spoken more politely!” Gao Yuan whispered.

“I asked him to pay,” Shi Feng replied. “Very politely.”

The landlord looked as if he might faint over someone else's courage.

A runner from an ordinary herb shop arrived before he finished packing. The shop canceled a prepared supply and returned his deposit. The runner wouldn't look at him while explaining.

“My owner says he can't promise the next lot,” Jiang Lu said.

“Did he already sell it?” Shi Feng asked.

“I don't know,” Jiang Lu replied quickly.

Shi Feng accepted the returned stones and let him leave. The young Qi Condensation runner wasn't going to argue with his own employer for a hooded stranger. There was no point frightening an answer out of him.

Three interrupted arrangements in one afternoon. Sima Yu's name made ordinary men abandon profit before a guard even drew a blade. Shi Feng felt anger, but it stayed clear instead of turning into helpless worry. He still had personal medicine, ingredients in storage, and enough cash to continue without begging the next customer for an advance.

This was why he stopped swallowing every spare stone into cultivation. A reserve gave him room to act when someone interfered. It couldn't stop royal pressure, but it could keep that pressure from deciding what he ate tonight.

Shi Feng packed his unused personal ingredients into the ring. He left the room tidy and paid the session's agreed balance. Gao Yuan didn't try to charge for the threatening visit.

For the first time, he appeared afraid of the answer. Shi Feng wasn't going to beg customers to risk royal punishment for his sake. He also wasn't going to offer his work, identity, and formulas for free because Sima Yu wanted them.

He thought, If he wanted ordinary profit, he could buy pills. He wants a hand around my throat.

The prince already tried killing Shi Feng. Now his servants wanted control of Master Shen. Whether Sima Yu proved the connection or only suspected it, the purpose was clear enough.

Shi Feng left by the main road and watched the people behind him. A man with a brown scarf stopped at the same stalls he did. Another waited near the west gate, looking away too late.

Not skilled shadows. Men confident their employer's name made care unnecessary.

He didn't confront them in the crowded street. Tomorrow afternoon, after his final furnace booking, the shortcut behind the old west-canal timber yard would give Zheng Jian all the quiet stone he wanted.

At home, Ling Qingzhu noticed he returned early with the medicine boxes still full.

“Bad sales?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Some orders changed,” Shi Feng replied.

“Then rest,” Ling Qingzhu said. “You always say you're busy.”

He looked at her and smiled faintly. Her answer was simple, and right now he appreciated that.

They sat beneath the pear tree while she read a passage from her book. He corrected one herb name, and she accused him of showing off. For a little while, the canceled orders stayed folded inside his bag.

After she went in, he checked the refined artifact sword. The channel answered his qi cleanly. He put it away beside the Returning Breath Pills and closed the ring's space.

Tomorrow evening wasn't a deadline he intended to obey. He had already refused. Another visit wouldn't turn refusal into permission, no matter whose name the visitor carried.

chapters.title: No One Left to Report
chapters.html:
“Going somewhere, Master Shen?” Zheng Jian asked.

Shi Feng stopped between the stacked cedar beams of the disused west-canal timber yard. At the furnace-lane sluice gate, Gao Yuan and the canal watchman had seen Zheng Jian and two Eastern Palace retainers follow the hooded alchemist into the yard. The retainers then pulled the chain across the alley gate.

Now they no longer bothered hiding.

Zheng Jian stood beside the dry saw-pit with a narrow refined artifact blade in his hand. A second man blocked the canal archway, his late Foundation Establishment aura spreading openly across the wet flagstones.

A third crouched atop a timber stack with a cocked hunting crossbow.

“Your deadline was evening,” Shi Feng said.

“You packed your shelves at noon,” Zheng Jian replied coldly. “I decided not to wait until you slipped out of the ward.”

The late Foundation Establishment retainer laughed. A thick scar crossed his shaved scalp, and his broad saber rested on one shoulder.

“Take off the cloth,” Peng Zhao said. “Let's see the face that thinks it can refuse the Eastern Palace.”

Shi Feng didn't move his hand toward the cloth.

“Does Sima Yu want a face or a corpse?” Shi Feng asked.

Zheng Jian's expression hardened at the prince's unadorned name, and Peng Zhao flicked two fingers toward the timber stack.

The iron quarrel hissed straight at Shi Feng's chest.

Shi Feng glided half a pace left so the bolt buried itself two inches deep in a cedar beam, and in the same breath he vaulted up the stacked timber. Before the Qi Condensation bowman could reach for his belt hook, Shi Feng's palm struck the man's bow-arm and chest.

Ribs gave way with a muffled crack. The bowman tumbled silently into the sawdust pit below and didn't rise.

Peng Zhao's laughter died.

His broad saber came down as Shi Feng landed, carrying a heavy wave of late Foundation Establishment qi aimed to cleave him from collarbone to hip.

A plain refined artifact sword appeared in Shi Feng's hand.

Piercing Current.

The narrow point slipped inside the saber's arc and sheared through Peng Zhao's shoulder guard. His defensive qi shattered on impact. Blood sprayed across the timber before he understood he'd been cut.

Peng Zhao staggered back, clutching his ruined shoulder.

“Early Foundation Establishment?” Peng Zhao rasped.

Shi Feng's qi was visible to him now. The stage was two steps below his own; the force behind the steel wasn't.

Zheng Jian went pale.

The steward's narrow blade darted toward Shi Feng's flank. Shi Feng pivoted with Turning Wave, parrying the edge so hard Zheng Jian's blade spun into the saw-pit, then stepped in and struck the steward's wrist with the flat of his sword.

Bone snapped.

Zheng Jian cried out and stumbled backward against the timber stack.

“Wait!” Zheng Jian shouted. “You haven't heard His Highness's full offer!”

“The crossbow explained it,” Shi Feng replied.

Behind him, Peng Zhao roared and lunged with his left hand, swinging the heavy saber toward Shi Feng's neck in a desperate final gamble.

Shi Feng stepped inside the swing, trapped the saber hilt beneath his forearm, and drove his free palm squarely into Peng Zhao's sternum. Completed golden bone met exhausted protective qi; Peng Zhao's chest caved inward, and the late Foundation Establishment killer dropped beside the saw-pit without another sound.

Zheng Jian stared at the body. Terror replaced the authority in his face.

A late Foundation Establishment hired killer died in only a few exchanges. Master Shen hadn't suffered a wound. The difference between them wasn't something a household badge could fix.

“I serve the Crown Prince,” Zheng Jian said hoarsely.

“I noticed,” Shi Feng replied.

“If I don't return, he'll investigate!” Zheng Jian cried.

“Then he should hire someone better,” Shi Feng said.

Zheng Jian dropped to one knee. His broken wrist hung against his robe, and he struggled to keep his breathing steady.

“We can still settle this,” Zheng Jian said. “Spirit stones. I'll give you everything on me.”

Shi Feng looked at him without warmth.

The man stood calmly while a crossbow aimed at his neck. His companion followed with a full killing blow. Now he wanted an ordinary bargain because the expected victim proved stronger.

“No,” Shi Feng said.

Zheng Jian's good hand flashed toward his belt. A small needle shot out, catching the light. Shi Feng caught that wrist too and drove the sword through his chest.

The steward sagged against the blade. His last attempted trick never reached its target. Shi Feng withdrew the steel and let him fall.

There was no one left to report his face, realm, or weapon.

He checked the canal wall first. The three men had chained the alley gate themselves so no passerby would interrupt their work.

The bowman carried spare bolts and a small payment pouch. Peng Zhao had recovery pills and silver-edged spirit coin. Zheng Jian's Eastern Palace waist plaque confirmed what Gao Yuan had already seen in the furnace yard.

Shi Feng kept the coin and pills, left Zheng Jian's Eastern Palace waist plaque beside the broken crossbow in the flooded culvert beneath the sluice where the canal dredge would find it, and left the inner gate chain untouched. When the ward constables questioned Gao Yuan and the sluice watchman, both witnesses would tell the same story: Zheng Jian had threatened Master Shen at the furnace room, followed him into the timber yard with two armed men, and chained the gate himself. Shi Feng slipped out over the back wharf wall.

No human corpse fed his physique. He didn't try.

By the time he finished, the sunlight shifted toward afternoon. The whole battle took far less time than cleaning up after the men who started it.

Shi Feng washed the sword and checked its channel. The plain refined artifact held well. His sword control kept the exchanges short, and the First Extreme supported far more force than the opponents could withstand.

He tested the Returning Breath Pill he kept for the day's practice. The medicine recovered the qi spent in the fight steadily, though the exchanges used far less than a long refining session. He felt no hidden ache in his body and found no wound beneath his robe.

Peng Zhao's higher stage gave him more qi than an ordinary early Foundation Establishment opponent. It didn't give him Shi Feng's meridians, completed Extreme, or foundation. Once the saber missed, the difference in their bodies decided the exchange.

Shi Feng checked the sword's point again and put it inside the ring. He returned the ordinary steel to his belt before stepping onto the wharf lane. A passerby would see a hooded man with a common weapon, not the battle that had ended behind the timber stacks.

He wasn't going to mistake that for permission to become careless. Still, three men below the kingdom's apex weren't a life-and-death crisis anymore.

He thought, Sima Yu will learn his servants didn't return. He can wonder why.

The prince remained behind household guards in the capital. Shi Feng would meet him on a different field soon enough. His orders weren't forgiven merely because today's messengers died first.

At home, Ling Qingzhu was trying to move the new flowerpot away from a patch of afternoon shade.

“Here?” Ling Qingzhu asked when he entered.

“Morning sun reaches there,” Shi Feng replied.

“That's what I thought,” Ling Qingzhu said.

She let him take the pot, although she could have lifted it easily herself. He moved it two feet to the side and set it down gently.

Ling Qingzhu watched his hand. There was a small smear of mud near his cuff.

“Practice again?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“Did it go well?” Ling Qingzhu asked.

“Very,” Shi Feng said.

She seemed satisfied. He went inside to wash, and she followed him to complain about the flower seller's watering advice.

He listened while folding the clean cloth from his retreat. The ordinary home sounds pleased him after the quiet timber yard.

No one knocked that evening to demand his formulas.

Shi Feng cooked supper with both hands steady. The prince could send another offer. He would receive the same answer.

chapters.title: What He Chose to Carry
chapters.html:
“You're still going to register,” Ling Qingzhu said.

Shi Feng looked up from the ordinary sword across his knees. “Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

The ten days since the notice were nearly over. Young cultivators filled the capital's inns, and every meal stall had someone explaining how qualification ought to work. At home, Ling Qingzhu kept returning to the same question.

He didn't blame her. She still believed his meridians were ruined.

“I won't ask them to let you pass,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“I didn't ask you to,” Shi Feng replied.

“Good,” Ling Qingzhu said. “Because that wouldn't help you once you're facing someone.”

“No,” Shi Feng agreed.

His agreement seemed to irritate her more than an argument would. She sat on the stool beside him and watched him check the scabbard's tie.

“You make it difficult to worry,” Ling Qingzhu said.

“Then stop,” Shi Feng replied gently.

She looked at him sharply. The softness in his voice made the answer harder to dismiss.

“I didn't say I was worried,” Ling Qingzhu muttered.

“Of course,” Shi Feng said.

He put the ordinary sword away. She stayed beside him, clearly unwilling to leave the matter there.

“If you can't meet the requirement, withdraw,” Ling Qingzhu said. “Don't let someone hurt you just because he says something unpleasant.”

“I won't,” Shi Feng replied.

That was the truth. A stranger's insults at the registration board weren't going to decide whether Shi Feng could fight. His strength already decided that.

He spent the next morning outside the capital with the refined artifact sword. The secluded clearing held fresh targets cut from fallen branches. No live tree needed to suffer because he wanted different heights.

Piercing Current reached the narrow gap between two sticks. The point passed cleanly without touching either side.

Turning Wave followed. He stopped the cut just before the edge reached the next target, then released the force elsewhere into the empty air.

The hardest part wasn't striking. It was stopping exactly where he intended.

Qualification didn't require killing every opponent. If the tenth-ranked candidate fought like a competitor, Shi Feng would defeat him like one. An actual attempt at murder would receive a different answer.

He didn't confuse a bad temper with a death sentence.
