Xiahou Lie tried the small shift with his good arm and immediately became serious.

“So that's where I lost it,” Xiahou Lie said.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

The body cultivator nodded as though the defeat had become useful at last.

“Don't become impossible to find,” Xiahou Lie said. “I dislike chasing people just to get hit.”

“You could stop asking for it,” Shi Feng replied.

Xiahou Lie laughed and went toward the treatment rooms. He didn't offer an oath of brotherhood or promise to follow Shi Feng into whichever sect he chose.

He wanted another fight. That was simple enough to respect.

Duan Yichen waited by the passage with Sima Lan. The princess looked at Shi Feng's hands, then toward Xiahou Lie's retreating back.

“His arm,” Sima Lan said.

“Will heal,” Shi Feng replied.

“I meant yours,” Sima Lan said.

Shi Feng opened and closed one hand.

“Still attached,” Shi Feng replied.

Duan Yichen laughed. Sima Lan gave him a cold look before turning toward the board.

The first semi-final place now carried Shi Feng's name.

Under the sect awning, He Zhen set his brush down and flexed his own fingers thoughtfully.

Mu Shuyun noticed.

“You're not entering the next match,” Mu Shuyun said.

“I was thinking about the angle,” He Zhen replied.

“Everyone saw the angle,” Wei Chengyuan said. “The strength behind it matters more.”

He Zhen didn't argue. The Martial Palace delegate was right about that much. A clever turn wouldn't stop Xiahou Lie unless the hand applying it could hold the body cultivator in place.

Shi Feng's visible mid Foundation Establishment cultivation wasn't the whole explanation.

That didn't mean He Zhen understood what else supported it. He simply wrote that the young man controlled his strength well.

A useful observation was better than inventing a divine physique from one match.

Wei Chengyuan looked toward Shi Feng's passage for a long moment. The young man already refused to answer an early invitation. Each victory would make the final answer harder to force.

That irritated him.

Shi Feng ate in the waiting courtyard while the platform was cleaned. Duan Yichen sat opposite him and complained that the tournament meals had fewer vegetables than the inn's.

“Then buy some,” Shi Feng said.

“The stall outside charges more today,” Duan Yichen replied.

“Become a champion. Complain afterward,” Shi Feng said.

“Ninth is the best I can do,” Duan Yichen answered.

Shi Feng looked at the sabre user's grin and felt his own mood ease a little. Duan Yichen wasn't pretending disappointment over a place he'd fought hard to earn.

That was good company.

Before standing, Shi Feng swallowed a pill from his own bottle. The medicinal force settled into his foundation cleanly. He wasn't injured, but the steady accumulation still mattered. His foundation needed far more than one tournament afternoon could provide, and he wasn't going to waste the official rest period arguing about other people's opinions.

He still noticed the empty seat beside them when a passing woman wore violet. The feeling lasted only a moment, but it remained sharp.

Ling Qingzhu was on her way to a new teacher. He hoped the journey was safe.

He didn't reach for paper to ask.

A bell sounded from the arena. The next quarter-final would begin shortly.

Duan Yichen finished the last bite and stood.

“Gongsun Ce's puppets first,” Duan Yichen said. “Then the swordswoman. Gu Zhan's been asking whether they can hurry.”

Shi Feng rose and adjusted the sword at his waist.

“Someone should tell him the others want to win too,” Shi Feng said.

“He knows,” Duan Yichen replied. “That's what he likes.”

They returned to the passage as the next names rang across the stands.

chapters.title: The Crown Prince of Great Qin Falls
chapters.html:
“Yuan Kuang,” Gu Zhan said. “I've been waiting.”

The crown prince of Great Qin looked at the spear across his opponent's shoulder. His peak Foundation Establishment aura pressed forward, heavy enough to make the loose dust drift across the centre mark.

Gu Zhan didn't seem to notice.

“Then don't waste the match talking,” Yuan Kuang replied.

Gu Zhan grinned. That was a good answer.

From the waiting passage, Shi Feng watched the two men take their positions. Gongsun Ce already defeated Cao Zhenyu in the previous quarter-final. The prince's sword couldn't reach the controller through the shifting line of puppets.

Bai Chenxi followed with a controlled victory against Tan He. Frost slowed the small-sect swordsman's steps until she forced his blade down and stopped her point against his shoulder.

The other semi-finalists were settled.

Now Yuan Kuang and Gu Zhan would choose the fourth.

Duan Yichen stood beside Shi Feng with his heavy sabre resting on the floor.

“Yuan Kuang was the favourite before the first round,” Duan Yichen said.

“Before people watched Gu Zhan,” Shi Feng replied.

“He'll hate hearing that,” Duan Yichen said.

“He doesn't need to hear it,” Shi Feng replied. “He's about to find out.”

Lu Yong announced the start.

Yuan Kuang drew a broad-bladed sword and attacked with a strong descending cut. His qi spread behind the edge, covering the space on either side so an ordinary retreat wouldn't clear it.

Gu Zhan stepped forward.

The spearhead struck the flat of the blade near its base. A short turn pushed the attack past his shoulder.

Yuan Kuang's expression changed. His first strike wasn't supposed to lose its direction so easily.

He recovered quickly and thrust at the chest.

Gu Zhan moved his left foot half a step. The blade passed beside his robe, and the spear's shaft struck Yuan Kuang's wrist.

The prince's fingers nearly opened.

“Hold it properly!” Gu Zhan shouted.

The shout wasn't an insult. He genuinely didn't want the weapon falling before the match became interesting.

That made it worse.

Yuan Kuang's face reddened. He pulled his sword back and released the full force of his peak Foundation Establishment cultivation.

A bright arc rose above the platform.

People in the front rows leaned away despite the protective boundary. The sword technique carried enough force to break an ordinary cultivator's guard in a single blow.

Gu Zhan watched it and looked pleased.

“That's more like it,” Gu Zhan said.

He lowered the spear from his shoulder, set both hands properly, and thrust.

There was no great circle of light. The spear travelled straight through the point where Yuan Kuang's technique gathered.

The bright arc broke apart.

Yuan Kuang staggered as the force scattered back through his weapon. Before he could plant his rear foot, the spear shaft struck his chest.

He flew across the boundary and landed hard outside the platform.

Gu Zhan remained at the centre.

He looked toward Lu Yong with visible disappointment.

“Already?” Gu Zhan asked.

“Out of bounds,” Lu Yong replied. “Gu Zhan wins.”

The stands erupted.

“Three exchanges!”

“Yuan Kuang couldn't make him retreat!”

“Martial Palace already praised that sword technique!”

“Look at the betting board!”

The betting board was being changed by a man who didn't look happy about it.

Yuan Kuang stood after a physician checked his chest. The blow hurt, but Gu Zhan hadn't tried to kill him.

That left him no excuse worth shouting.

Gu Zhan approached the edge and offered the fallen sword hilt first. Yuan Kuang accepted it with a stiff expression.

“You could've followed the first cut faster,” Gu Zhan said.

“I know how to use my own sword,” Yuan Kuang replied.

“Then why didn't you?” Gu Zhan asked honestly.

The prince stared at him.

From the passage, Duan Yichen covered a laugh with a cough. Shi Feng didn't bother hiding his small smile.

Gu Zhan wasn't good at comforting defeated opponents. He wasn't even aware that comfort might be expected.

Yuan Kuang took the sword and walked away before the spear user offered another lesson.

Under the sect awning, Wei Chengyuan's expression had become unpleasant. His promised disciple lost without showing the strength he'd praised so loudly.

Mu Shuyun looked at the spear still held in Gu Zhan's hand.

“Lone Spear Peak keeps its name honestly,” Mu Shuyun said.

He Zhen nodded. Then he looked toward Nie Wufeng in the upper stands.

The old master was peeling a piece of fruit with a short knife. He barely raised his head when the crowd shouted the result.

He didn't seem surprised at all.

Gu Zhan found Shi Feng outside the waiting area.

“Did you watch?” Gu Zhan asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“The third cut was worth taking seriously,” Gu Zhan said.

“So you ended it,” Shi Feng replied.

“It didn't get better afterward,” Gu Zhan said, sounding disappointed again.

Duan Yichen folded his arms.

“You ended it before finding out,” Duan Yichen said.

Gu Zhan considered that, then nodded.

“Next time I'll ask first,” Gu Zhan said.

“Please don't,” Duan Yichen replied. “Some of us would like to lose without answering questions.”

Shi Feng laughed softly. The sound surprised him. For a few moments, the afternoon didn't feel entirely occupied by what he'd left behind.

The hurt hadn't vanished. There was simply something else happening around it.

Zhou Ke approached with the next set of match tokens. He handed one to Shi Feng and another to Gu Zhan.

“Semi-finals after the rest period,” Zhou Ke said. “Shi Feng against Gongsun Ce. Gu Zhan against Bai Chenxi.”

Gu Zhan looked toward the swordswoman's waiting place and grinned.

“Good,” Gu Zhan said. “She doesn't fall over when the wind changes.”

Shi Feng checked his own token. Gongsun Ce's puppets required attention, but not fear. He'd already watched enough exposed qi lines to know where he should begin looking.

Gongsun Ce stood beyond the passage checking a puppet's shoulder. The prince didn't look disappointed that his next opponent noticed the work. He simply tightened the joint, tested its movement, and closed the case. Shi Feng liked that calm. It promised a cleaner match than another grand speech about birth.

He put the token away and rested his hand on the plain sword's hilt.

chapters.title: Semi-final: The Third Prince
chapters.html:
“Don't mistake the puppets for separate opponents,” Gongsun Ce said.

Shi Feng stood across from three wooden figures and their controller. The third prince's late Foundation Establishment qi moved along thin visible lines between the puppet cores.

“I won't,” Shi Feng replied.

“Good,” Gongsun Ce said. “People usually keep hitting the first one.”

The prince opened a narrow case and placed two small refined artifacts beside his feet. Each carried a simple feeding channel connected to the puppet lines.

Shi Feng watched carefully. Mo Tianheng's alchemy knowledge didn't make every artifact in the world familiar. But qi moving from a supply point toward a working core followed rules he understood.

Xu Changhe's modest diagrams taught him where ordinary connections needed protection. His own furnace practice taught him to notice when a supply weakened during a change.

That was enough to begin.

He didn't need to become a grandmaster refiner in the time it took Lu Yong to raise his hand.

“Begin,” Lu Yong said.

The first puppet charged.

Its wooden fist struck where Shi Feng stood a breath earlier. The second figure turned across the first one's side, closing the space his retreat opened.

The third waited behind them with both hands raised.

Shi Feng stepped left and touched the first puppet's elbow with his sword. The joint held. It was reinforced more carefully than the exposed wood suggested.

Gongsun Ce smiled faintly.

“Not there,” Gongsun Ce said.

“I noticed,” Shi Feng replied.

A small artifact beneath the prince's feet lit up. The third puppet released a short burst of qi through its palms, forcing an ordinary opponent to retreat into the first two figures.

Shi Feng moved through the gap before it closed.

The blast passed behind him. His robe fluttered, but the force didn't threaten his body. He could've destroyed the nearest puppet with a much stronger blow.

He chose not to.

Breaking everything by brute force would tell the delegates more than he wanted them to know. Cutting the exposed supply would end the match just as clearly.

He needed the right moment.

The first puppet struck again. Shi Feng met the wrist with the flat of his sword and turned the arm outward. The second figure moved to cover it, just as before.

This time, he watched the line between their cores.

It brightened before the third puppet fired.

There.

Shi Feng stepped forward and used Piercing Current through the narrow opening. His sword didn't attack a wooden chest. It cut the unprotected copper connector beneath the first puppet's rear shoulder.

The figure stopped.

Its raised fist remained hanging in the air.

Gongsun Ce's expression changed.

“He cut the feed,” He Zhen said beneath the sect awning.

Wei Chengyuan looked at the stopped puppet, then at the thin connection hanging beneath its shoulder.

“An exposed point,” Wei Chengyuan said.

“Yes,” He Zhen replied. “After he forced the turn.”

Mu Shuyun leaned forward slightly. She didn't know the puppet's entire design, but the reasoning was clear. Shi Feng watched a repeated movement, created the same opening, and cut the part that carried qi through it.

He didn't need to understand every artifact on the platform.

Gongsun Ce moved the remaining two puppets apart and changed their rhythm.

The third prince wasn't finished.

A metal ring on Gongsun Ce's wrist glowed. The second puppet stopped covering the first and drove straight toward Shi Feng.

The third moved behind it.

Shi Feng caught the change and retreated one step. His sword turned a heavy wooden fist aside. The impact made the inexpensive blade ring more sharply than he liked.

Still usable. Don't meet another one there.

He lowered the sword and changed his target.

Gongsun Ce's small feeding artifact stood only a few paces behind the moving figures. When the third puppet fired, a visible pulse passed from the artifact into its core.

The line ran close to the stone.

Shi Feng drew the second puppet toward him, stepped across its leading foot, and struck its knee from the side with his palm.

The figure stumbled.

It didn't break. It didn't need to.

For one breath, its own body blocked the prince's view of the low feeding line.

Turning Wave swept beneath the wooden hip and cut the narrow connector near the ground.

The third puppet's hands dimmed before the next blast formed.

Gongsun Ce pulled his wrist back sharply. Shi Feng was already moving past the stumbling figure.

Returning Tide brought the blade back toward the prince's hand.

The point stopped against the glowing metal ring.

Gongsun Ce looked at the blade, then at his two disabled puppets. The third stood between them, active but badly placed to stop a sword already within the controller's guard.

The prince sighed.

“I surrender,” Gongsun Ce said.

Shi Feng withdrew at once.

The audience erupted when Lu Yong confirmed the result.

“He didn't break the puppets!”

“He cut two little pieces!”

“That last figure was still moving!”

“It couldn't reach him!”

Gongsun Ce crouched beside the first damaged connection. He examined the clean cut and shook his head.

“I should've covered that,” Gongsun Ce said.

“It needed room to turn,” Shi Feng replied.

“Then a wider cover,” Gongsun Ce said.

“Then slower turning,” Shi Feng replied.

The prince considered the problem seriously. Losing the match apparently hadn't damaged his interest in the puppets.

“You've given me work,” Gongsun Ce said, running a thumb over the severed copper feed. “Artificer Hall holds an inner-court mechanism trial every autumn. If we both end up on that mountain, don't expect the next return channel to sit where your sword can reach it.”

“You brought three people to hit me today,” Shi Feng replied. “Bring four in the autumn.”

Gongsun Ce laughed for the first time that afternoon.

Shi Feng helped him lift the stopped figure clear of the passage. The damage was limited to ordinary fittings. Repairing it would cost time, not the whole puppet.

That suited both men.

At the entrance, Duan Yichen waited with the next official notice.

“The final,” Duan Yichen said.

“One opponent left to decide,” Shi Feng replied.

“Gu Zhan's been smiling since your match began,” Duan Yichen said.

Shi Feng looked toward the other passage.

The one-eyed spear user raised his weapon in greeting, then pointed eagerly toward Bai Chenxi's platform.

He clearly intended to settle that last question quickly.

chapters.title: Semi-final: Frost and Spear
chapters.html:
“Your sword's cold,” Gu Zhan said.

Bai Chenxi looked at the frost gathering along her guard. Her peak Foundation Establishment qi was steady, and her expression didn't change at the obvious observation.

“Then don't touch it,” Bai Chenxi replied.

Gu Zhan grinned and placed the spear in both hands.

“That sounds better,” Gu Zhan said.

The crowd settled as Lu Yong raised his hand. Bai Chenxi had defeated every previous opponent without losing control of her method. Gu Zhan made a royal favourite look clumsy in three exchanges.

Neither would give the stands a quiet match.

Shi Feng watched from beside the passage with Duan Yichen. He rested a hand on the plain sword's hilt and waited to see how the spear user handled the spreading frost.

Lu Yong announced the start.

Bai Chenxi moved first. Her sword drew a low line across the platform, and pale frost spread behind the point. She didn't aim to freeze the whole arena. She closed the paths Gu Zhan was most likely to use.

The spear user watched the edge of the frost and stepped into it.

His first thrust met her sword directly.

The weapons rang. A white crack spread through the frozen stone beneath her leading foot.

Bai Chenxi slid backward, stopped, and raised the guard again.

Gu Zhan looked delighted.

“You held it!” Gu Zhan shouted.

Bai Chenxi didn't answer. She turned the retreat into a short cut toward his wrist.

The spear shaft rose and stopped the blade.

Gu Zhan's grin remained, but his clear eye followed her fingers carefully. He enjoyed the match. He wasn't careless about it.

The second exchange began before the spectators finished shouting about the first.

Bai Chenxi sent a thin wave of frost upward along the spear shaft. Gu Zhan loosened one hand, turned the weapon, and struck the creeping ice against the edge of her sword.

The frost broke.

A short thrust followed through the scattered white pieces. Bai Chenxi moved her head aside, but the point touched the clasp at her collar before she could regain distance.

Gu Zhan stopped.

“You can yield,” Gu Zhan said.

Bai Chenxi looked at the spearhead, then at him.

“Move it,” Bai Chenxi replied.

He pulled the weapon back, honestly surprised that the match wasn't finished.

She immediately changed her stance.

Duan Yichen leaned forward beneath the awning.

“She's going to use the whole frost field,” Duan Yichen said.

Shi Feng nodded. The retreat planted several thin lines of ice across the stone. Bai Chenxi hadn't wasted the earlier movement, even while losing the exchanges.

It was a good method.

Gu Zhan saw it too. His expression became more eager, not less.

The swordswoman brought the blade down.

Frost rose around his legs from three sides. The nearest ice gathered in a sharp ridge, meant to turn his next step toward her waiting sword.

Gu Zhan stamped once.

His qi burst through the weak point where the three lines met. The ice shattered before it closed, and the spear swept across the opening.

Bai Chenxi blocked. The force pushed her close to the boundary.

Gu Zhan stopped again.

“Now?” Gu Zhan asked.

Bai Chenxi's wrist trembled. She tightened her grip until it steadied.

“No,” Bai Chenxi replied.

The spear user looked genuinely puzzled.

“You can't stop the next one,” Gu Zhan said.

“Then show me,” Bai Chenxi replied.

He nodded, as though that finally explained the matter.

The third stroke was simple.

Gu Zhan stepped forward and thrust through the centre of her guard. Bai Chenxi met the shaft with the flat of her sword, but the force behind it turned the blade aside.

The spear stopped beneath her chin.

Her next step would've crossed the boundary. Her sword couldn't return in time.

She lowered it slowly.

“I surrender,” Bai Chenxi said.

Gu Zhan withdrew immediately.

“Good fight!” Gu Zhan said.

His happiness was so open that the defeated swordswoman couldn't decide whether to feel more annoyed or relieved.

She chose to bow and leave before he offered another exchange.

Lu Yong confirmed the result. The crowd erupted beneath the two final names.

“Shi Feng against Gu Zhan!”

“The sword and the spear!”

“Neither's shown his limit!”

“Who bet against Lone Spear Peak?”

Several people became very quiet after that last question.

Mu Shuyun met Bai Chenxi at the passage entrance. She checked the young woman's wrist and nodded once.

“No lasting damage,” Mu Shuyun said.

“I know,” Bai Chenxi replied.

“You didn't need the third exchange,” Mu Shuyun said.

“I wanted to see it,” Bai Chenxi answered.

The Hundred Flower Valley delegate smiled faintly. That was a better reason than refusing to surrender because a crowd was watching.

“Rest properly,” Mu Shuyun said. “There's still a third-place match.”

Bai Chenxi flexed her fingers once and considered where the spear broke through. Gu Zhan didn't destroy the whole frost field. He struck the place where her own lines gathered.

She needed to hide that point better.

The thought steadied her disappointment. Losing wasn't pleasant, but she didn't have to leave with nothing except an injured pride. If she corrected the method, the three exchanges would remain useful long after the crowd forgot them.

Bai Chenxi looked toward Gongsun Ce's waiting area. The prince was checking a replacement connector beneath one puppet's shoulder.

She would need her wrist steady for that.

Gu Zhan approached Shi Feng as soon as the official released him.

“Tomorrow,” Gu Zhan said.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“Don't fight like Yuan Kuang,” Gu Zhan added.

“I wasn't planning to,” Shi Feng said.

“And don't stop after finding one opening,” Gu Zhan said. “Try another!”

Duan Yichen looked at the spear user with pity.

“You're asking him to hit you more?” Duan Yichen asked.

Gu Zhan nodded enthusiastically.

“If he can,” Gu Zhan said.

Shi Feng smiled. The man's skill was worth watching, and his eagerness made a pleasant change from hidden threats.

But his strength still wasn't Shi Feng's true limit.

That distinction belonged to Shi Feng alone.

“Rest first,” Shi Feng said.

Gu Zhan glanced at the spear, clearly disappointed that it wasn't already tomorrow.

chapters.title: A Letter from the Valley
chapters.html:
“A letter for Shi Feng,” Zhou Ke said.

Shi Feng stopped beside the reporting desk. The attendant held a narrow envelope with Hundred Flower Valley's mark across the outer fold.

Shi Feng accepted it and signed. The handwriting on the smaller inner fold was familiar enough that he didn't need to turn it over twice.

Ling Qingzhu.

He put the letter away before leaving the busy hall. Several candidates were arguing over tomorrow's viewing seats. A merchant wanted the official to confirm whether his expensive platform cushions were allowed.

The ordinary noise continued while Shi Feng walked through it.

At the inn, he closed his room's door and set the sword beside the table. Then he opened the envelope.

The first page began with the youth review in Great Liang's capital.

“I was sixteen when I first saw you, a month after your test,” Ling Qingzhu wrote. “Your household had brought you after the public test of two hundred and thirty-seven meridians. You stood beside Lu Qingxue. The prince wasn't at the review, but his household's steward offered you patronage in front of everyone. People moved aside before he finished speaking. They thought your answer had already been decided.”

The next paragraph continued beneath it.

“You thanked him and put the patronage token back. When he waited for you to bow, you asked whether he wanted your answer or your forehead. Then you left with Lu Qingxue. I had never seen anyone refuse them so calmly. I remembered it long after the others stopped discussing your meridians. You didn't notice me. I know that now.”

The handwriting filled the second page too.

“You fetched Lu Qingxue's tea before taking your own. She wore a white-jade pin you'd given her, and you moved her cup away from an elbow before it spilled. I was jealous of Lu Qingxue at the review. I'm still a little jealous now. It was foolish to envy a cup of tea, but I knew you hadn't done those things because anybody ordered you to.”

“I heard how you ended the engagement. You changed the paper, refused the stones and didn't say a bitter word about her. When I saw you in Sky Pavilion square, I wanted to know whether the man from the review was still there. He was. Your fall made it possible to approach you without handing my clan to another faction. It wasn't what made me want to approach you.”

The final paragraphs were shorter.

“I told you why I needed a husband. I didn't tell you why I wanted that husband to be you. I called it convenience because admitting more would have let you refuse something I couldn't blame on politics. That was my pride. It doesn't excuse how I treated you afterward. The repayment settled the stones. It didn't settle the times you told me the truth and I chose not to listen.”

“I reached the Valley safely. The teacher is strict, and the instruction is useful. I hope your final goes well. You needn't answer this.”

Ling Qingzhu had signed beneath the last line.

Shi Feng read the letter once, folded both pages along their creases, and put them inside his spatial ring.

He didn't take out paper for a reply.

Duan Yichen found him in the inn courtyard later that afternoon. The sabre user carried two bowls from the kitchen and looked pleased with himself.

“Plain food,” Duan Yichen said. “The innkeeper stopped calling it a champion's meal after I asked whether he included a champion.”

Shi Feng accepted one bowl.

“You're improving,” Shi Feng said.

“At ordering food?” Duan Yichen asked.

“At not paying for the name,” Shi Feng replied.

They ate beneath the narrow shade. The inn was busier now, with visitors hoping to glimpse the finalists before the next morning.

Duan Yichen ignored the people peering through the gate. He was studying the list of Martial Palace's training methods he'd received after the placement match.

“They offered you a place?” Shi Feng asked.

“Not the final papers yet,” Duan Yichen replied. “They're making certain I know how fortunate I should feel.”

“You are fortunate,” Shi Feng said.

“I know,” Duan Yichen replied. “I just don't need them to explain it between every two bites.”

Shi Feng smiled. Ninth place was a real opening for the sabre user. Being grateful for it didn't require losing every ordinary opinion he possessed.

They finished without turning the silence into a problem.

After Duan Yichen left, Shi Feng went to the medicine street for one small purchase. His sword needed fresh binding near the hilt. The old strip loosened after repeated matches, and he didn't want to notice it under a spear tomorrow.

Tan Gu, the shopkeeper, was at Qi Condensation and knew enough about weapons to keep the pitch short.

“Grip cloth or leather?” Tan Gu asked.

“Leather,” Shi Feng replied.

“Soft?” Tan Gu asked.

“Not when wet,” Shi Feng said.

The shopkeeper handed him a plain strip and named an ordinary price. Shi Feng paid, thanked him, and left.

Back at the inn, he removed the old binding and checked the hilt beneath it. The weapon was inexpensive, but he'd learnt its weight and the way its edge accepted qi.

It had brought him through the earlier rounds without demanding a greater name.

He wrapped the new strip tightly, tested the grip, and set it aside.

Then he cultivated.

His own pills strengthened the foundation without resistance. He guided the medicine steadily, waited for the gain to settle, and checked the next morning's reporting time.

Then he opened Xu Changhe's sword notes. Returning Tide depended on recovering the blade without leaving the wrist open. He repeated the shortened turn beside the bed, slowly enough to stop before the edge reached the wall.

Duan Yichen had warned him about Gu Zhan's second thrust. The warning needed practice, not another conversation. Shi Feng adjusted his rear foot and tried the turn again. The sword came back closer to his arm.

He put the notes away when the movement stopped pulling his shoulder forward.

Near sunset, Zhou Ke passed the inn with a final reminder for both finalists. Shi Feng met him at the gate and accepted the written time.

“Rest tonight,” Zhou Ke said. “The stands won't forgive either of you for sleeping through the bell.”

“I'll arrive,” Shi Feng replied.

“Gu Zhan asked whether he could arrive early,” Zhou Ke added.

“How early?” Shi Feng asked.

“Now,” Zhou Ke said.

Shi Feng looked toward the distant arena roofs and shook his head.

“Tell him the platform won't run away,” Shi Feng said.

“I did,” Zhou Ke replied. “He said that wasn't what he was worried about.”

The attendant left with a tired expression. Shi Feng went back inside and closed the gate before the curious visitors could invent another reason to enter.

On the table, the sword lay ready beneath its new binding.

The letter remained in the ring.

chapters.title: Two Old Men in the Stands
chapters.html:
“You're sitting on my bag,” Li Changyuan said.

Nie Wufeng looked down at the shabby bundle beneath his elbow. A bent wooden wheel poked through one side.

“Then stop putting rubbish on seats,” Nie Wufeng replied.

He moved the bundle anyway. Li Changyuan sat beside him with a quiet grunt, then opened a packet of roasted beans.

The arena below was nearly empty. Workers repaired the marks left by the semi-finals while attendants checked the protective pillars for the final morning.

Neither old man watched the repairs with much interest.

For a while, they ate beans without speaking.

Then Nie Wufeng turned his head and examined his neighbour's plain robe.

“Still dressing like you lost your own luggage,” Nie Wufeng said.

“Still eating like the army owes you a meal,” Li Changyuan replied.

Nie Wufeng's hand stopped above the packet.

Both men looked at each other properly.

Then the spear master's expression changed into a broad, surprised grin.

“You old bastard,” Nie Wufeng said.

“You haven't become polite,” Li Changyuan replied.

“Not for you,” Nie Wufeng said.

They laughed quietly enough that the workers below didn't look up.

The laughter faded when Nie Wufeng looked toward the northern sky.

“I thought you stayed near the wall,” Nie Wufeng said.

“Which wall?” Li Changyuan asked.

“The Empire's northern one,” Nie Wufeng replied. “Don't pretend a fence outside Qingyun City took that scar.”

Li Changyuan pulled his sleeve lower across an old mark near the wrist.

“Walls stay where they're built,” Li Changyuan said. “People don't have to.”

Nie Wufeng considered that and nodded. He didn't ask for a full account of the intervening years, and his old acquaintance didn't offer one.

There were names neither wanted to say in a public stand.

“Your army still owes me a spear,” Nie Wufeng said.

“It wasn't my army,” Li Changyuan replied.

“You signed for the supplies,” Nie Wufeng said.

“You broke six spears in one week,” Li Changyuan replied. “I remember the complaint.”

“Bad spears,” Nie Wufeng said.

“Bad temper,” Li Changyuan answered.

Nie Wufeng laughed again. The old memory lost some of its heaviness without becoming a story for everyone passing the seats.

Li Changyuan offered the beans. Nie Wufeng took another handful and looked down toward the platform.

“Your interest is the boy with the sword?” Nie Wufeng asked.

“He understands why things break,” Li Changyuan said.

“He'll have an interesting morning,” Nie Wufeng replied.

“So will your one-eyed fool,” Li Changyuan said.

Nie Wufeng looked pleased by the insult.

“He'd be offended if you called him cautious,” Nie Wufeng replied.

Shi Feng entered the lower stand while Zhou Ke was checking the next morning's entrance route. He wanted to see the final platform's repaired edge before the crowd filled every passage.

He wasn't studying a way to escape Gu Zhan. He was checking where he could move without driving a restrained exchange into the protective boundary too early.

Zhou Ke pointed at the newly marked corners.

“Same rules,” Zhou Ke said. “No changes because it's the final.”

“Good,” Shi Feng replied.

“Your opponent asked whether the officials would stop a long match,” Zhou Ke added.

“Did you answer?” Shi Feng asked.

“I said we'd stop it when someone lost,” Zhou Ke replied.

Shi Feng smiled. Gu Zhan was making everyone explain ordinary things as though tomorrow's fight might disappear through a careless rule.

He turned to leave and noticed Li Changyuan above the lower stair.

The shabby old man waved him over.

“Still buying broken tools?” Shi Feng asked as he approached.

“Someone has to keep them away from fools,” Li Changyuan replied.

Nie Wufeng looked between them with growing amusement.

“You know each other?” Nie Wufeng asked.

“He saw the crack in a puppet core,” Li Changyuan said.

“It wasn't hidden very well,” Shi Feng replied.

“The seller didn't see it,” Li Changyuan said.

“The seller didn't want to,” Shi Feng answered.

Nie Wufeng laughed and moved the bundle off the third seat. Shi Feng sat for a moment without asking either old man to become his teacher.

Nie Wufeng looked at the plain sword at Shi Feng's waist.

“Gu Zhan will ask you not to end it quickly,” Nie Wufeng said.

“He's already asked,” Shi Feng replied.

“Of course he has,” Nie Wufeng said.

“Should I ask him the same thing?” Shi Feng asked.

The spear master smiled.

“He won't enjoy losing,” Nie Wufeng said. “He'll enjoy finding out why.”

That sounded right. Shi Feng liked the distinction. Gu Zhan could want victory without treating every stronger opponent as an insult.

Li Changyuan passed him the packet of beans.

Shi Feng accepted a few. Ordinary roasted beans, still warm from whichever stall sold them. No mysterious medicine hid beneath the paper.

He appreciated that too.

“Did you repair the core?” Shi Feng asked.

“No,” Li Changyuan replied. “I opened it.”

“To see the damage?” Shi Feng asked.

“To see what the damage showed me,” Li Changyuan said. “A working thing hides plenty of its maker's mistakes.”

Shi Feng nodded. That was useful advice without becoming another demand for gratitude. He'd learnt enough from failed pills to understand the point.

“Have you chosen a sect?” Li Changyuan asked.

“I'll answer when the offers come,” Shi Feng replied.

“That's sensible,” Li Changyuan said. “Listen carefully. Some people spend more effort naming what you'll receive than explaining what they'll expect.”

“I've met merchants,” Shi Feng replied.

Nie Wufeng nodded solemnly.

“Some of them sit on better chairs,” Nie Wufeng said.

Li Changyuan kicked his foot lightly. The spear master laughed and protected the beans from spilling.

Shi Feng stood when the workers began closing the lower passage. He returned the packet and nodded to both old men.

“Tomorrow,” Nie Wufeng said.

“Tomorrow,” Shi Feng replied.

He left them beneath the empty seats, still arguing over whether a broken wheel counted as useful luggage.

Only after his footsteps faded did Nie Wufeng turn toward Li Changyuan again.

“You're going to enjoy this,” Nie Wufeng said.

Li Changyuan looked down at the waiting platform.

“I already am,” Li Changyuan replied.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.html:
“Join Martial Palace,” Wei Chengyuan said. “The Yunze matter disappears.”

Shi Feng sat across from him in a private room above the arena offices. Two cups stood untouched between them. The delegate's late Golden Core aura remained concealed, but everyone outside the door knew whom the room belonged to.

“The matter Wen Shou already heard?” Shi Feng asked.

“Wen Shou serves Great Liang,” Wei Chengyuan replied. “The Wei branch has its own dead to remember.”

“Their elder attacked first,” Shi Feng said.

“I read the account,” Wei Chengyuan replied.

“Then read it again,” Shi Feng said.

The delegate's expression cooled. He'd expected refusal to require coaxing, not a reminder that his threat wasn't an honest accusation.

“You're talented,” Wei Chengyuan said. “Talent still needs a place to grow. Some roads close when a young man chooses badly.”

Shi Feng looked at the untouched tea.

“So that was an offer,” Shi Feng said.

“It was advice,” Wei Chengyuan replied.

“Keep it,” Shi Feng said.

He stood without waiting for permission. Wei Chengyuan didn't rise. His fingers rested beside the cup, and his gaze followed the plain sword at the young man's waist.

“You won't always be fighting juniors on a protected platform,” Wei Chengyuan said.

Shi Feng stopped beside the door.

“Then don't always speak as though I am,” Shi Feng replied.

He left before the delegate could turn the same threat into a fourth polite sentence.

Outside, the evening air felt cooler than the room.

Shi Feng walked through the busy street without looking back. Wei Chengyuan's strength was real. A late Golden Core expert was a genuine danger he couldn't take lightly at his current realm.

That didn't mean he needed to accept a sect chosen through a threat.

He hadn't tried to kill the delegate for insulting him. The man hadn't attacked. But the warning was clear, and Shi Feng would remember who delivered it.

The Yunze deaths weren't suddenly a crime because someone powerful wanted a useful disciple.

Shi Feng thought, Finish tomorrow first. Then choose my own road.

At the inn, Kang Liu asked whether he wanted a larger meal before the final. Shi Feng ordered an ordinary supper and paid the named price. The owner looked pleased enough that he didn't try to explain what champions ought to eat.

Duan Yichen joined him near the end of the meal.

“Martial Palace sent for you,” Duan Yichen said.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“A good offer?” Duan Yichen asked.

“A loud one,” Shi Feng said.

The sabre user studied his expression, then put down the question. He wasn't obliged to share every opinion of the sect he might enter, and Shi Feng wasn't going to choose his future for him.

“They've offered me a place after the final papers,” Duan Yichen said.

“Earn what you can from it,” Shi Feng replied. “Don't stop thinking after you enter the gate.”

Duan Yichen nodded seriously.

“I won't,” Duan Yichen said.

They finished supper without turning the conversation into an oath against every person in Martial Palace.

Shi Feng checked his sword before lying down. The new grip binding held well, and the edge showed only the ordinary wear of several matches.

His pills were packed separately from the travel provisions. He swallowed one from his own stock and let its strength settle through the foundation.

The late stage was approaching through accumulation, not grief or tomorrow's applause. He didn't need to force it before the final to be confident.

Mid Foundation Establishment was enough.

He put the bottle away and extinguished the lamp.

Three breaths later, someone knocked hard enough to shake the door.

“Shi Feng!” Gu Zhan called. “Are you asleep?”

“Not anymore,” Shi Feng replied.

He opened the door. The one-eyed spear user stood outside with his weapon in hand and an expression much too cheerful for the hour.

“I found a better angle,” Gu Zhan said.

“For knocking?” Shi Feng asked.

“For the thrust after your first turn,” Gu Zhan replied.

Shi Feng looked at the spearhead. Gu Zhan immediately lifted it clear of the door frame, having noticed the possible misunderstanding.

“Not here,” Gu Zhan added. “Tomorrow.”

“Good,” Shi Feng said. “Go to bed.”

“Can't,” Gu Zhan replied. “Tomorrow's too good.”

Shi Feng let him sit in the courtyard rather than explaining sleep through a closed door. Gu Zhan used a twig to draw two lines in the dust.

“Your sword comes back here,” Gu Zhan said. “If I turn the shaft first, I can stop it there.”

“You're telling your opponent?” Shi Feng asked.

“I want to know what you'll do,” Gu Zhan replied.

“Tomorrow,” Shi Feng said.

Gu Zhan stared at the lines and looked briefly disappointed. Then the disappointment became excitement again.

“Good,” Gu Zhan said. “Don't tell me.”

Shi Feng leaned back with his arms folded. He'd spent the evening listening to one man hide threats beneath advice. Now another man openly explained the attack he hoped to use against him.

He much preferred the second conversation.

Gu Zhan drew a third line, scratched it out, and began talking about Bai Chenxi's frost field. His questions were precise whenever the fight interested him. He wasn't a fool. He simply didn't care about many things other people found important.

At last, Shi Feng took the twig away.

“Enough,” Shi Feng said. “You have a match tomorrow.”

“So do you,” Gu Zhan replied.

“Which is why I'm going to sleep,” Shi Feng said.

Gu Zhan considered arguing. Then he stood and picked up the spear.

“Don't oversleep,” Gu Zhan said.

“Don't knock again,” Shi Feng replied.

The spear user laughed and left through the gate. Kang Liu watched from the front hall with visible relief that nobody practised inside his courtyard.

Shi Feng returned to his room and closed the door.

He checked the window latch and tested the repaired sword grip with a short thrust. The leather stayed tight beneath his palm. He lowered the blade, laid it beside the bed and relit the lamp to check the reporting time once more.

He lay down and slept.

chapters.title: Third Place
chapters.html:
“You repaired the connectors,” Bai Chenxi said.

Gongsun Ce opened the puppet case and lifted the first wooden figure onto the platform. A narrow metal cover now protected the shoulder point Shi Feng cut in the semi-final.

“I didn't enjoy the first repair,” Gongsun Ce replied. “I'm avoiding a second.”

Bai Chenxi drew her sword. Her peak Foundation Establishment qi spread in a pale layer along the edge.

“Then I'll find something else,” Bai Chenxi said.

The prince smiled and set the other figures beside the first. His late Foundation Establishment cultivation was lower than hers, but the puppets gave him more than one place to apply it.

Lu Yong checked both candidates and announced the start.

Frost spread across the platform immediately.

Bai Chenxi didn't waste time trying the same direct approach Shi Feng used. She couldn't copy his speed and strength simply because she watched the match.

She chose the puppets' feet instead.

The first figure advanced. Ice gathered beneath its leading sole and made the step shorter than Gongsun Ce intended.

Bai Chenxi moved past its shoulder.

The second puppet turned to intercept. She struck its wrist, pushed the arm low, and thrust toward the controller behind it.

Gongsun Ce raised one hand. The third figure stepped across the opening with both wooden arms folded.

Her sword hit its reinforced guard and rang sharply.

Bai Chenxi retreated before the first puppet's fist reached her back.

Shi Feng watched from the finalists' passage.

Duan Yichen stood beside him, still looking pleased whenever the attendants called him ninth instead of referring to his defeat by Gu Zhan.

“She can't reach him,” Duan Yichen said.

“She reached him once,” Shi Feng replied. “He used the third puppet to close it.”

“Can she freeze all three?” Duan Yichen asked.

“She'd spend too much qi keeping them still,” Shi Feng said. “The controller only needs one opening while she does it.”

On the platform, Bai Chenxi changed her method.

She drove a narrow line of frost along the first puppet's knee rather than spreading it across the whole floor. The joint slowed. Her next cut struck beneath its arm and exposed a dark seam.

Gongsun Ce pulled that figure back at once.

The second came forward while the third moved to his left. Their positions changed too quickly for the swordswoman to finish the damaged knee.

She frowned and gathered more qi.

The prince's repaired covers did what he wanted. They weren't impossible to break, but each extra cut gave the other two figures time to move.

That was enough.

The match continued through several strong exchanges.

Bai Chenxi's frost forced Gongsun Ce to keep changing the paths he used. Gongsun Ce's puppets forced her to spend more qi moving between them than striking the controller.

Neither method dominated immediately.

The crowd enjoyed that. After Gu Zhan's quick victory and Shi Feng's clean cuts through the feeds, a long struggle made them feel they finally had time to understand what they were watching.

“She's slowed the first one again!”

“The other two are covering him!”

“Watch her sword!”

“He moved before she finished!”

Gongsun Ce stepped sideways and let the second puppet take a glancing cut. The blade tore a strip of wood from its shoulder.

Bai Chenxi saw the opening and thrust.

This time, the third puppet didn't move in front of the prince.

It moved behind her.

She noticed the shadow and turned before its fist landed. That saved her from the heavy blow, but it carried her sword out of line with Gongsun Ce.

The prince lifted the wrist ring.

The first puppet, slowed but not stopped, struck the flat of her blade with both hands.

Her injured wrist trembled.

A second figure stepped into the space beside her elbow. Its wooden fist stopped an inch from her ribs.

Bai Chenxi looked at it, then at the controller beyond her sword's reach.

“I surrender,” Bai Chenxi said.

The puppets stopped immediately.

“Gongsun Ce wins,” Lu Yong declared. “Third place, Gongsun Ce. Fourth place, Bai Chenxi.”

The prince recalled the figures and checked the new shoulder damage. Bai Chenxi cleaned a few splinters from her sword edge.

“You left the third one's path open deliberately,” Bai Chenxi said.

“Yes,” Gongsun Ce replied.

“You waited until I watched your hand,” Bai Chenxi added.

“You were the dangerous part,” Gongsun Ce said. “I couldn't ignore your sword to worry about the floor.”

She accepted that without becoming pleased by a compliment. The answer described the match honestly enough.

“Next time, the wrist ring first,” Bai Chenxi said.

Gongsun Ce covered it with his other hand and smiled.

“Please don't tell everyone,” Gongsun Ce replied.

They bowed and left opposite sides of the platform. Neither needed to turn the result into a personal grudge.

Sima Lan watched the prince pack the damaged puppet. She examined the movement of the repaired shoulder, clearly interested in what changed after Shi Feng's match.

Gongsun Ce noticed her gaze.

“The cover held,” Gongsun Ce said.

“The other shoulder didn't,” Sima Lan replied.

He looked at the loose strip of wood and sighed.

“There's always another repair,” Gongsun Ce said.

Shi Feng heard the exchange as he passed and almost smiled. Artificer Hall would probably have plenty of work for a prince who disliked leaving a broken joint alone.

The attendants cleared the platform and checked the protection again. Two final name plates were carried beneath the central banner.

Shi Feng. Gu Zhan.

Gu Zhan stood so close to the entrance that Zhou Ke had to wave him back twice.

“Not yet,” Zhou Ke said.

“I know,” Gu Zhan replied.

He took one step back and continued staring at the platform.

Shi Feng adjusted the binding on his sword and watched the last repair crew leave. His body was rested and his qi steady. He had watched the spear throughout the gathering, but watching it was no substitute for meeting it. He checked the new grip once more and walked toward the passage.

Above them, the final bell began to ring.

For the first time all morning, even Gu Zhan stopped talking.

chapters.title: The Final: One Eye, One Spear
chapters.html:
“Don't disappoint me,” Gu Zhan said.

Shi Feng drew the plain sword and checked the distance between them.

“You've asked often enough,” Shi Feng replied.

The spear user grinned. His clear eye was bright, and the qi around his weapon was denser than it looked the previous afternoon.

Lu Yong examined him carefully before announcing anything.

“Half-step Golden Core,” Lu Yong said.

The front rows reacted immediately. Gu Zhan stood at the transition beyond peak Foundation Establishment, with his qi beginning the final change before a core formed.

He hadn't entered a new major realm yet.

That distinction mattered to the officials and meant very little to the excited spectators.

“He's already at the threshold!”

“Against mid Foundation Establishment!”

“Can Shi Feng stop that spear?”

“Look at the old master!”

Nie Wufeng was sitting with his arms folded. He didn't seem interested in helping the crowd decide how frightened it should be.

Shi Feng drew his qi through the full length of the blade and steadied his stance.

Gu Zhan's half-step Golden Core pressure carried a razor-sharp spear intent forged through a hundred real fights. Even with his completed golden bones and three hundred and sixty-five meridians, Shi Feng knew this wasn't an opponent he could beat with half-measures.

“Begin,” Lu Yong said.

Gu Zhan attacked at once.

The spear came straight toward Shi Feng's throat, then turned toward his shoulder before the sword could meet it.

Shi Feng changed the blade's angle and caught the shaft near the head. The impact drove him half a step back before he could turn the spear clear.

The crowd gasped.

Gu Zhan laughed.

“Good!” Gu Zhan shouted.

He pulled the spear back and thrust again before the first impact stopped ringing. Shi Feng turned the point aside and returned a short cut toward the forward hand.

Gu Zhan changed his grip exactly as he'd described in the inn courtyard.

The spear shaft knocked the returning sword away.

Shi Feng smiled. So the man really used the angle he'd spent half the night discussing.

Then he'd give him another one to think about.

Piercing Current drove beneath the lifted shaft. Gu Zhan stepped back before the point reached his chest, but the movement cost him the centre mark.

Shi Feng followed at once, gathering more qi behind the next stroke.

The next exchange ended with both weapons held between them. The spear pushed downward. The sword slid sideways, refusing the direct contest of strength the audience expected.

Gu Zhan's expression became serious.

The sword was quieter than Xiahou Lie's fists and more troublesome than Yuan Kuang's bright attacks. Every short movement tried to change where his next thrust could begin.

He liked it enormously.

Bai Chenxi stood beneath the far awning with her sword sheathed. She watched Shi Feng step past a thrust that forced her to retreat in their earlier match.

He didn't move farther. He moved sooner.

That difference annoyed her because it was easy to describe and difficult to copy. She tried the small foot turn without drawing her blade, then stopped when it pulled at the sore wrist.

Training could wait until the injury healed.

For now, watching properly would have to be useful enough. She fixed her attention on Gu Zhan's forward hand before the next attack began.

Duan Yichen leaned against the passage rail, watching without speaking.

Sima Lan stood beside Gongsun Ce. The prince had left the repaired puppet case with an attendant rather than trying to carry it through the packed waiting area.

“Neither's given an opening,” Sima Lan said.

“They've given several,” Gongsun Ce replied. “Neither's accepted the wrong one.”

On the platform, Gu Zhan let his forward foot drift close to the boundary. Shi Feng saw the invitation and refused to drive him out through the obvious path.

The spear was already waiting across that path.

Instead, Shi Feng stopped and struck the shaft near Gu Zhan's rear hand.

The one-eyed cultivator twisted aside, laughing again.

“You saw it!” Gu Zhan shouted.

“You left it there,” Shi Feng replied.

The crowd grew louder. Each clash rang like a forge hammer across the arena.

On the fourteenth exchange, Gu Zhan pivoted on his rear heel and drove the iron-wood spear butt squarely into Shi Feng's braced left forearm as Shi Feng parried the point.

A sharp, metallic crack echoed inside Shi Feng's sleeve. For the first time since he had completed the First Extreme in the Hengyun ridge hut, a hairline fracture scored the surface of his golden radius bone. His left fingers numbed for half a breath as his boots skidded two paces across the flagstones.

Shi Feng's eyes lit with fierce focus. Across from him, Gu Zhan grinned from ear to ear.

The spear user changed his rhythm.

Three quick thrusts came high, low, and straight through the centre. Shi Feng stopped the first, avoided the second, and met the third with a short turn of the wrist.

The inexpensive sword rang sharply.

He shifted the contact nearer the hilt before the thinner part of the blade took too much pressure.

The weapon had a real limit. He'd remember that.

Gu Zhan advanced, delighted to find that the exchange hadn't ended. His qi flowed more freely with every thrust. The dense force near his centre gathered instead of scattering after the attack.

Nie Wufeng sat forward.

Li Changyuan noticed the movement from the next seat.

“Now?” Li Changyuan asked quietly.

“He's never been patient,” Nie Wufeng replied.

Below them, Gu Zhan struck the sword aside and raised the spear for another thrust. Then his body stopped before the weapon moved.

The expression on his face changed.

Shi Feng stepped back at once.

He felt the qi gathering too quickly to remain ordinary Foundation Establishment circulation. Gu Zhan's force was condensing around a newly forming centre.

A Golden Core.

The air above the platform grew heavy. Several banners snapped against their poles despite the still morning beyond the arena walls.

Lu Yong moved forward immediately.

“Both candidates, stop!” Lu Yong ordered.

Shi Feng lowered the sword without arguing. Gu Zhan looked up at the darkening sky, then down at his spear with obvious irritation.

“Now?” Gu Zhan demanded.

Nobody answered that question for heaven.

The first low thunder rolled above the arena.

chapters.title: Tribulation Over the Arena
chapters.html:
“Clear the platform,” Lu Yong ordered.

The attendant beside the entrance moved immediately. Shi Feng stepped through the passage with his sword lowered, leaving Gu Zhan at the centre beneath the gathering clouds.

The spear user looked annoyed enough to argue with the sky.

“Can we finish first?” Gu Zhan asked.

“No,” Lu Yong replied.

Gu Zhan sighed and planted the spear beside his foot.

Above him, the clouds darkened. The heavy pressure wasn't a technique released by a candidate. Gu Zhan's breakthrough had drawn the lightning tribulation that came with entering Golden Core.

People in the nearest rows scrambled back despite the protective pillars.

Lu Yong raised both hands and directed the arena protection toward the stands. The surrounding delegates helped clear the open aisles, ensuring nobody stood where a stray discharge could reach them.

They didn't place a shelter above Gu Zhan.

His tribulation belonged to him.

Nie Wufeng remained in his seat, watching with his arms folded. His disciple looked toward him once.

“Master?” Gu Zhan called.

“What?” Nie Wufeng asked.

“Will the match wait?” Gu Zhan asked.

The old man stared at him for a moment.

“Survive first,” Nie Wufeng replied.

Gu Zhan looked reassured, which wasn't the response most people would've expected.

The first bolt struck the centre of the platform.

Gu Zhan lifted the spear and drove his qi through it. White light swallowed his shoulders. The stone beneath his feet cracked, and a harsh sound tore through the arena.

When the light faded, he was still standing.

His robe smoked along one sleeve. His clear eye remained fixed on the clouds.

“Again!” Gu Zhan shouted.

Duan Yichen gripped the rail beside Shi Feng.

“He says that to everything,” Duan Yichen muttered.

Shi Feng watched the qi gathering near Gu Zhan's centre. The first bolt strengthened the condensation rather than destroying it. The spear user wasn't trying to avoid the change. He was driving through it with the same directness he brought to every fight.

That suited him.

The next lightning strike came harder.

Gu Zhan lowered his stance and met it with the spear shaft across both hands. The force drove him down to one knee. The platform cracked wider beneath the impact.

Several spectators cried out.

Nie Wufeng didn't move.

Gu Zhan rose through the fading light with blood at the corner of his mouth. He wiped it away impatiently and shook his burned sleeve clear of the forward hand.

The injury was real. So was the force forming inside him.

Nobody offered a pill or sent a stronger cultivator onto the platform to take the next strike for him.

He would enter Golden Core by passing what heaven sent, or fail there under the clouds.

Shi Feng stood quietly beside the passage while the following strikes fell.

Inside his sleeve, the hairline crack along his golden left radius bone throbbed warmly as he circulated his qi through all three hundred and sixty-five meridians to knit the golden marrow. Once Gu Zhan crossed into early Golden Core, holding back would mean losing.

The crowd didn't know that.

They looked from the tribulation to Shi Feng with growing sympathy. A mid Foundation Establishment finalist now seemed destined to face an opponent an entire major realm above him.

Some already expected him to withdraw.

Sima Lan watched his calm expression and frowned.

“You don't look surprised,” Sima Lan said.

“He was at the threshold,” Shi Feng replied.

“That isn't what I meant,” Sima Lan said.

“I know,” Shi Feng replied.

She stopped asking. Whatever else he possessed, she wasn't going to extract it with a question beneath a thundercloud.

Duan Yichen leaned closer instead.

“You'll still fight?” Duan Yichen asked.

“Yes,” Shi Feng said.

The sabre user nodded once. He was worried, but he didn't begin explaining that surrender was sensible before Shi Feng even saw the changed spear.

That was appreciated.

The last strike drove Gu Zhan's spear point deep into the stone.

For a breath, nobody could see his body through the lightning. Then the white light broke apart and rose toward the thinning clouds.

Gu Zhan stood with one hand around the embedded shaft.

His breathing was rough. Burns marked the robe and skin beneath it. But the scattered qi around him slowly drew inward, settling around a stable centre.

Early Golden Core pressure spread across the platform.

The stands erupted.

“He passed!”

“A Golden Core before the final ends!”

“Lone Spear Peak has another expert!”

“What happens to the match?”

Gu Zhan was already pulling the spear from the stone when Lu Yong stepped onto the edge.

“Sit,” Lu Yong ordered.

“The clouds are gone,” Gu Zhan replied.

“Your qi isn't settled,” Lu Yong said.

Gu Zhan looked as though that was an unnecessarily slow concern. He sat anyway.

The official pause lasted until his new cultivation held steady. Gu Zhan used his own recovery medicine, guided the qi carefully, and stopped trying to stand every time an attendant passed.

More than an hour passed before the new qi stopped surging with every breath. The burns remained, but the worst of the pain eased beneath Gu Zhan's own medicine.

He wasn't entering the resumed match untouched. He also wasn't too injured to stand properly. Lu Yong made him walk the repaired edge and perform one controlled thrust before allowing another argument about starting early.

Gu Zhan obeyed, then looked toward Shi Feng again.

Lu Yong examined the result himself before addressing the arena.

“Eligibility was verified on entry,” Lu Yong announced. “A lawful breakthrough during the gathering does not cancel it. Both finalists may resume once the platform is safe.”

Workers cleared loose fragments from the centre. The protection around the stands remained active, but no tribulation cloud returned.

Gu Zhan rose at last and looked toward Shi Feng.

There was a little uncertainty beneath his usual eagerness.

“You'll still come?” Gu Zhan asked.

Shi Feng drew the sword and walked toward the entrance.

“I haven't left,” Shi Feng replied.

The spear user's grin returned immediately.

Lu Yong checked the repaired footing, looked at both candidates, and raised his hand again.

chapters.title: The Extreme
chapters.html:
“Begin,” Lu Yong said.

Gu Zhan's spear crossed the platform before the echo faded.

Early Golden Core qi gathered along the head, sharper and denser than the force he used before the tribulation. Shi Feng caught it on the flat of his sword and felt the change through his wrist.

The inexpensive blade cracked.

Its outer half spun away, struck the protective boundary, and fell onto the stone. The shock tore the skin between Shi Feng's right knuckles. He stepped aside before the continuing thrust reached his chest.

Gu Zhan pulled back immediately.

“Take another sword from the rack!” Gu Zhan called.

Shi Feng glanced at the ordinary weapons beyond the passage. None would withstand repeated contact with this spear. Changing one weak blade for another would only postpone the same problem.

He still had half his own sword. He knew its weight.

“No need,” Shi Feng said.

He flexed his left fingers. The golden radius bone cracked before the tribulation still ached beneath the sleeve. His qi had eased the numbness during the pause, but the fracture hadn't healed.

One hard blow there would matter.

Across from him, Gu Zhan settled the spear into both hands. The burns along his sleeve remained, but his new Golden Core qi was steady.

“Then come on!” Gu Zhan said.

Shi Feng raised the jagged half-blade.

The next thrust drove him backward.

Shi Feng turned the point aside near his remaining guard. Gu Zhan changed his grip before the broken blade could reach the forward wrist. The shaft swept across Shi Feng's chest and forced him to duck.

He tried to advance under it.

The spearhead returned faster than before.

A thin line of blood opened across Shi Feng's ribs. He twisted clear before the cut deepened, but the sudden pain broke his next step. Gu Zhan drove forward and took the centre from him.

Shi Feng retreated twice.

The boundary lay three paces behind his heel.

Duan Yichen gripped the passage rail. Sima Lan stopped breathing for a moment as the next spear flash crossed the space in front of Shi Feng's throat.

“He's losing ground!”

“The sword can't reach!”

“One more retreat and he's out!”

Shi Feng heard them. They weren't wrong.

Gu Zhan wasn't an ordinary opponent whose cultivation alone explained his strength. Years of spear practice gave him a clean answer to every attempt to shorten the distance. The breakthrough made those answers faster and heavier.

Shi Feng needed to change how he entered.

Meeting the point again wouldn't do it.

He planted his rear foot and struck the shaft from below with Piercing Current. Gu Zhan lifted his forward hand, letting the shortened blade pass beneath the weapon.

Then the rear end came around.

Shi Feng caught it on his left forearm.

Pain shot to his shoulder.

The hairline fracture in the golden radius opened wider. His left fingers went numb, and the impact drove his heel across the stone until it stopped a hand's width inside the boundary.

Gu Zhan didn't pause.

The spear turned toward his heart.

Shi Feng dropped his left shoulder and drove his right foot inward.

The point tore through loose cloth instead of his chest. He struck toward Gu Zhan's wrist with Turning Wave, forcing the spear user to move the forward hand back.

For the first time since the sword broke, the gap shortened.

Gu Zhan stepped away immediately. His other hand pulled the shaft through, and the spearhead turned back toward Shi Feng before the sword could follow.

Shi Feng tried Returning Tide.

The jagged blade hooked the inner guard, but Gu Zhan turned his wrist and broke the contact. A burst of early Golden Core qi threw Shi Feng's weapon arm wide.

The next thrust grazed his shoulder.

Blood darkened the robe.

Shi Feng staggered, caught his footing, and dragged the half-blade back between them. The spear point stopped against the remaining steel with a shrill ring.

He couldn't keep paying for each failed entry with another cut.

He thought, The shaft. Stop the shaft before he can change its reach.

His left hand was the only free one.

He forced qi through the numb fingers and felt them answer, slowly at first. The cracked bone hurt with every movement. It still held his arm together.

The First Extreme wasn't an excuse to ignore damage. It gave him one chance an ordinary body couldn't take.

He had to use it properly.

Gu Zhan watched him recover and grinned with fierce excitement. His own breathing was rough now. The resumed match had demanded more than the earlier victories combined.

“Still coming?” Gu Zhan asked.

Shi Feng set the broken blade close to his chest.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

Shi Feng watched the forward hand rather than the spearhead. Each time Gu Zhan shortened his grip, the rear foot followed before the next thrust. Catching the shaft while both hands were close would only let him pull the weapon free.

He needed the longer attack.

Shi Feng lowered the half-blade enough to expose the line beside his shoulder. It wasn't a harmless invitation. If his turn came late, the Golden Core point would enter before his injured hand reached the shaft.

He took one steady breath and waited.

In the stands, Nie Wufeng's fingers closed around his knee.

“He's leaving the centre open,” Nie Wufeng said quietly.

Li Changyuan watched the blood running from the young man's left sleeve.

“He needs the spear closer,” Li Changyuan replied.

Neither old man moved. The choice belonged to the two fighters, and the match wasn't finished.

Gu Zhan saw the opening and drove the spear straight through it.

Shi Feng moved toward it.

He didn't try to outrun the point. He turned just far enough that the spear aura sliced across his injured forearm rather than entering his ribs.

Then his bare left hand closed around the shaft behind the head.

The impact nearly tore the grip open.

Blood ran between his fingers. The fractured radius rang with pain, and his left knee bent under the force. He drove qi through all three hundred and sixty-five meridians and pulled his body into one braced line.

The two hundred and six golden bones answered together.

His hand held.

The spearhead stopped short of his heart.

Gu Zhan's eye widened. He twisted the shaft, trying to break the blood-slick grip before the half-blade could reach him.

Shi Feng turned with it instead of resisting the whole wrench through the cracked arm. His feet crossed inside Gu Zhan's forward step.

Piercing Current carried the jagged blade toward the inner wrist.

Gu Zhan released that hand and reached to strike.

Turning Wave changed the short thrust into a cut across the guard. The released hand jerked aside. Before it could return, Returning Tide brought the broken point beneath Gu Zhan's jaw.

Steel touched skin.

A bead of blood appeared.

Shi Feng stopped the blade there.

Gu Zhan's countering palm was still above the champion's shoulder. His spear remained trapped in Shi Feng's left fist, unable to finish its thrust.

The point had arrived first.

One more inch would've ended the fight permanently.

Gu Zhan looked down at the blade. His raised hand slowly lowered.

“I yield,” Gu Zhan said.

Shi Feng released the shaft only after Lu Yong stepped between them. His left arm shook as the pressure left it. The half-blade lowered in his right hand, and he drew a long, ragged breath.

“Shi Feng wins!” Lu Yong declared. “Champion of the Great Kingdom Tournament—Shi Feng of Great Liang!”

The stands exploded.

Gu Zhan sat down among the broken stones, breathing hard. Then he laughed, delighted and disappointed at once.

“You caught it,” Gu Zhan said.

“My sword broke,” Shi Feng replied.

“That last step,” Gu Zhan said. “I was late.”

Shi Feng nodded. He couldn't have afforded another failed entry either. The blood on his robe and the shaking arm made that clear enough.

“Again,” Gu Zhan said. “Someday. Soon?”

“When I have a better sword,” Shi Feng replied.

Lu Yong called the physicians forward. One began supporting Shi Feng's injured forearm while another examined Gu Zhan's burns and the shallow cut beneath his jaw.

Gu Zhan rose when the physician finished and retrieved the broken sword tip from the boundary. He gave it to Shi Feng without another challenge.

Above them, attendants lifted the final name plate.

Only Shi Feng's name stood at the top.

chapters.title: The Champion of One Hundred and Eight
chapters.html:
“Five thousand spirit stones,” Lu Yong announced. “Six Clear Essence Pills. And the champion's right to choose direct inner-disciple entry.”

Shi Feng accepted the sealed reward case with both hands. The official watched him check the seal and nodded, apparently pleased that someone remembered rewards were useful things rather than a reason to make a speech.

The stands were still shouting.

A mid Foundation Establishment cultivator defeated a newly advanced early Golden Core opponent. The broken sword made the result more dramatic, not less.

People who spent the morning explaining why he should surrender now tried to remember whether they actually said it aloud.

“I knew the sword would win!”

“You said the spear!”

“I said I'd watch the spear!”

“Then you watched him lose!”

Shi Feng looked toward the final board and felt a clear satisfaction.

He'd come for the choice. He earned it.

The exact force behind his victory remained unknown. So did his restored meridian count, the grade of his foundation, and the physique that made so much cultivation medicine usable.

The crowd didn't need those secrets to understand the result on the board.

Gu Zhan stood beside the runner-up mark with his spear resting against one shoulder. He accepted his own prize, then immediately examined the point as though the last exchange might've left a useful clue there.

Lu Yong finished the announcements before the spear user could ask for another platform.

Under the sect banners, attendants prepared the recruitment lists.

He Zhen stared down at Shi Feng's bloodied left hand and the broken half-sword with undisguised astonishment. A mid Foundation Establishment youth had just locked an early Golden Core spear in place with his bare fingers and finished the exchange with Xu Changhe's Returning Tide.

Beside him, Mu Shuyun let out a quiet breath. “The physical foundation beneath that boy's realm is monstrous.”

“The offers tomorrow will have to change,” He Zhen said, his brush trembling slightly over Artificer Hall's modest allotment sheet.

Wei Chengyuan looked toward the champion leaving the centre. The Martial Palace delegate's expression remained polite enough for the public, but his fingers tightened around the folded recruitment paper.

He'd already offered more than a country boy should've expected before the final. Now the young man could demand an answer from any of the three sects without accepting the same conditions.

That was inconvenient.

Several spectators nearby were discussing Hundred Flower Valley's early invitation to Ling Qingzhu.

“The wife left with an inner-disciple offer. The husband wins one himself!”

“Great Liang sent more than a prince this year!”

“Where will he go?”

Nobody answered the last question accurately. Shi Feng hadn't announced the decision.

Everyone had seen Ling Qingzhu's peak Foundation Establishment sword qi in Round Two, and the Valley's early inner-court offer gave the stands plenty to talk about without knowing the private foundation beneath it.

Her deepest talent remained her own.

Duan Yichen met Shi Feng at the passage and held out one hand.

Shi Feng took it. The sabre user pulled him into a brief shoulder bump and laughed openly.

“Champion,” Duan Yichen said.

“Ninth,” Shi Feng replied.

“Don't make mine sound smaller,” Duan Yichen said.

“It is smaller,” Shi Feng answered.

Duan Yichen laughed harder and released him before the reward case could be knocked loose.

“You'll need a sword,” Duan Yichen said, looking at the shortened weapon.

“Yes,” Shi Feng replied.

“A good one this time,” Duan Yichen added.

“A good price would help too,” Shi Feng said.

Sima Lan approached before the sabre user could begin naming every shop in the city. Her shoulder was wrapped beneath the Moon Lake robe, and her face looked less tired after the rest.

“Congratulations,” Sima Lan said.

Shi Feng nodded.

“You earned your place too,” Shi Feng replied.

“Barely,” Sima Lan said.

“The board doesn't add an apology beside tenth,” Shi Feng said.

She glanced toward it and smiled faintly. He was right. Her name stood among the ten recruits, without a note explaining that she almost failed.

That mattered more than looking magnificent in the process.

Gu Zhan joined them carrying the spear and a packet of food someone had pressed into his hand.

“Rematch when the new sword's ready,” Gu Zhan said.

“Not today,” Shi Feng replied.

“I didn't say today,” Gu Zhan protested.

Duan Yichen looked at him.

“You thought it,” Duan Yichen said.

Gu Zhan considered denying that and decided not to waste the effort.

At the inn, Kang Liu was waiting beside a freshly swept entrance. He looked at the prize case, then at Shi Feng's face, then back at the prize case.

“The champion stays here!” Kang Liu announced.

“To whom?” Shi Feng asked.

The innkeeper glanced at three guests who were openly listening from the front hall.

“To everyone,” Kang Liu admitted.

“No extra charges,” Shi Feng said.

“No extra charges,” Kang Liu promised quickly.

He'd already discovered that a famous guest could attract customers without being personally persuaded to pay more for a cabbage view.

Shi Feng went upstairs before the owner developed a longer speech.

Three business invitations waited beneath his room's door. One requested Golden Core medicine from the newly certified 1 Mark alchemist. The other two asked for bulk recovery pills before their caravans left.

He checked the dates and put the papers aside.

The first request named a formula he couldn't yet make reliably. The other orders would tie him to the city beyond the recruitment period. His success didn't make either promise sensible.

He wrote brief refusals rather than accepting advance payments he'd later need to return. Becoming rich required useful work, not collecting obligations faster than he could fulfil them.

Inside, he placed the reward case beside the sword. Five thousand spirit stones were useful. The Clear Essence Pills were more interesting immediately.

They were meant to support Foundation Establishment cultivation, and the seal guaranteed their proper preparation. He checked one carefully before putting it back.

His foundation was already near the next stage through months of pills, practice, and steady assimilation. The prize offered more medicine for a change he'd earned before the crowd began shouting.

He wouldn't swallow everything in a rush simply because today ended well.

Shi Feng washed, ate a proper meal, and left a message that he wasn't receiving visitors for the evening.

Then he sat beside the closed window and opened the pill bottle.

For the first time since leaving Great Liang, thinking about tomorrow gave him something clear to look forward to.

chapters.title: Late Foundation Establishment
chapters.html:
“One evening without knocking,” Shi Feng said.

Kang Liu looked at the closed room behind him, then at the note in his hand.

“Even if a sect delegate comes?” Kang Liu asked.

“They can leave a message,” Shi Feng replied.

“Even if Gu Zhan comes?” Kang Liu asked.

“Especially then,” Shi Feng said.

The innkeeper nodded, relieved to have a clear instruction for the visitor most likely to carry a spear through his front hall.

Shi Feng shut the door and checked the window latch. The room was clean, the sword pieces were packed away, and his cultivation medicines rested within reach.

Beneath the clean bandage on his left forearm, the hairline crack in his golden radius bone hummed with a fierce, living heat. Fighting an early Golden Core spear user at the edge of his strength had shaken loose the final barrier between mid and late Foundation Establishment. With the Clear Essence Pill prize in hand, tonight was the moment to break through.

He swallowed the first Clear Essence Pill and guided its medicinal force through the meridians.

The successful pill multiplied the effect of its ingredients. Its strength entered cleanly, without the resistance another cultivator might develop after frequent use.

Shi Feng absorbed it patiently.

His foundation needed more medicine than an ordinary one. That wasn't a sudden problem discovered after winning. He'd lived with the demand through every paid commission and every retained share.

Now the stored qi was close to completing the next change.

He let the first portion settle before taking another pill from his own accumulated stock. There was no reason to force the prize medicine through before the previous gain assimilated properly.

The process required control, not suffering.

Outside, footsteps crossed the corridor. Kang Liu's voice stopped a visitor near the stairs and explained that the champion was resting.

Shi Feng didn't listen for the reply.

He drew the medicinal qi inward and kept the flow even.

Hours passed.

The late stage didn't arrive with lightning or a heaven-shaking crack above the inn. Foundation Establishment didn't demand the Golden Core tribulation Gu Zhan passed that morning.

As the Clear Essence Pill's medicinal force surged through all three hundred and sixty-five meridians, it poured first into the hairline fracture in his left radius bone. The golden bone knitted shut, denser and brighter than before, and the combat insight from clashing head-on with Gu Zhan's early Golden Core spear fused with his accumulated qi.

With a deep inner resonance, the barrier gave way and the new stage settled into place.

Late Foundation Establishment.

Shi Feng opened his eyes.

His first feeling was satisfaction. His second was curiosity about how much finer the new qi would make the same alchemy method in his hands.

The final had tested his mid Foundation Establishment cultivation to its limit. The cracked arm showed where his control failed under the spear's pressure. Correcting that failure and assimilating the prize medicine carried the accumulated qi through the next barrier.

He'd won before the breakthrough.

The new stage simply extended his road.

Shi Feng stood and flexed one hand. A light pressure moved through the room, then disappeared when he withdrew it.

The table remained where it belonged. The window didn't explode. He had enough control to enter a new stage without buying the innkeeper another roof.

That pleased him almost as much.

He tested the finer qi through a short alchemy control sequence without lighting a furnace. The threads held their shape more easily. One split into two clean lines, then gathered again without scattering.

That would help the Golden Core formula he'd passed at Sky Pavilion. It wouldn't grant mastery of every medicine served by the same Mark.

Shi Feng wrote the change down before dressing. He wanted a proper practice session when the recruitment was settled, with enough ingredients to test the new control honestly.

His cultivation and alchemy could improve together. Neither needed a crowd to confirm the gain.
